summary: Background. Frailty is often raised as a reason to withhold complete revascularization from older patients after myocardial infarction, although the FIRE trial found no interaction between frailty and the benefit of physiology-guided complete revascularization. Objective. To estimate the cost-effectiveness of physiology-guided complete versus culprit-lesion-only revascularization after successful culprit-lesion percutaneous coronary intervention in patients aged 75 years or older with myocardial infarction and multivessel disease, overall and across Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) strata, from the German statutory health insurance perspective. Methods. A three-year cohort model with quarterly cycles was anchored to the FIRE marginal outcomes (primary composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke or ischaemia-driven revascularization 22.9% versus 29.8%; cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction 12.8% versus 18.2%; heart-failure hospitalisation 14.3% versus 19.7%). Risks in CFS 1-3, 4 and 5-9 were obtained by external calibration that preserved these trial marginals, with a relative treatment effect common to all strata. Costs used 2026 German diagnosis-related-group tariffs. Every input was classified by provenance, and uncertainty was assessed with 20,000 probabilistic draws, one-way and scenario analyses, and break-even analysis. Results. Complete revascularization cost EUR 757 more per patient and yielded 0.056 additional quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of EUR 13,601 per QALY. Ratios were EUR 20,541 per QALY in CFS 1-3, EUR 8,640 in CFS 4 and EUR 8,662 in CFS 5-9. The probability of cost-effectiveness at EUR 30,000 per QALY was 92.5% overall and 78.6%, 96.5% and 97.7% across strata. At that value, the minimum three-year absolute reduction in the primary composite required for cost-effectiveness was 4.3 per 100 patients overall, against a modelled trial effect of 6.9. Staging the additional procedure as a separate admission was the most influential cost driver. Conclusions. Within three years, physiology-guided complete revascularization appears cost-effective at reference values of EUR 20,000 to EUR 50,000 per QALY, and estimated cost-effectiveness was not attenuated in the frailer strata. The stratum-specific estimates rest on external frailty calibration rather than on frailty-specific FIRE outcomes and are not evidence of effect modification.
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Physiology-Guided Complete Revascularization Across Frailty Strata in Older Patients with Myocardial Infarction: A German Analysis Informed by the FIRE Trial

summary: Revision of the dataset prepared during peer review of the accompanying data descriptor at IEEE Data Descriptions . The 94 satellite–in-situ pairs and their concentration values are unchanged; what changes is how records are identified in time, what per-reservoir metadata is provided, and what guidance ships with the raw processor columns. Breaking change samples.csv no longer has a Date column. It is replaced by Campaign , with the values Summer YYYY and Autumn YYYY . The monitoring network samples these reservoirs twice a year, in June and in November, and the campaign label is what the compiled matchup table retains; the literal dates in v1.0.0 were a downstream conversion and should not be read as acquisition timestamps. Code written against v1.0.0 must be updated. Per-record acquisition timestamps were not retained when the table was compiled, so the individual in-situ/satellite temporal offsets cannot be recovered from these files. What is documented is the characterisation reported with the original processing (Cuartero et al., 2023): all 94 images fall inside the ±48 h selection window and 26% were acquired on the same day as the in-situ sample. Records cannot be filtered by temporal offset; studies for which simultaneity is critical should treat the whole collection as subject to an offset of up to two days. Added metadata.csv gains two morphometric descriptors per reservoir (15 → 17 columns): Eq. width (pix) , the equivalent width √A in 10 m pixels, and Window fraction (%) , the share of the water surface covered by a single 7×7 extraction window. Across the network the window fraction ranges from 0.26% to 49%. Users are advised to discard or treat separately any reservoir above about 25%. baseline_correction.py , a self-contained script (NumPy and pandas only) that fits a log–log correction log10(Chl) = a·log10(P) + b for each processor, plus a joint form over the three co-registered retrievals, and evaluates it under leave-one-reservoir-out cross-validation. Out-of-sample, it brings C2X from 639% to 39% MAPD and C2XC from 2181% to 43%; the joint form reaches 18%. It is a starting point and a sanity check, not a recommended retrieval, and its coefficients should not be transferred to other networks without refitting. Changed README updated for the new columns and the script, with a provenance note on time and a note on modelling with unevenly sampled reservoirs (Gini 0.32; effective number of equally weighted reservoirs 21.9 of 32). Use the reservoir, not the record, as the unit of resampling. The dataset is now named C2NEx-22, and the accompanying descriptor is identified as submitted to IEEE Data Descriptions .
title: C2NEx-22: A Paired Satellite–in-situ Chlorophyll-a in Extremadura, Spain for 32 Reservoirs Dataset

summary: This record contains the complete R and Python code and supporting documentation for the independent sensitivity reanalysis associated with the manuscript “Swab-based stool collection largely preserves gut microbiome structure with small device-dependent effects: an intra-individual evaluation of sampling devices and processing conditions.” The archive includes scripts to reconstruct and validate anonymous sample metadata from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) run report and FASTQ filenames; perform preliminary read-quality and paired-read overlap assessments; process forward (R1) and reverse (R2) reads separately using DADA2; infer ASVs; assign taxonomy using the SILVA SSU NR99 release 138.2 training set; construct phylogenetic trees; evaluate sequencing-depth dependence; calculate standardized alpha- and beta-diversity metrics, including Faith’s phylogenetic diversity, weighted UniFrac, and Bray–Curtis dissimilarity; compare the R1 and R2 results; assess sensitivity to rarefaction depth and unusually long terminal branches; and generate the corresponding tables and figures. The archive also contains a complete execution guide, software dependencies and versions, random seeds, original R session information, reference-database details, and file-integrity checksums. Sample metadata and analytical outputs are generated locally by the documented workflow and are not distributed as precomputed files. Raw paired-end sequencing data are publicly available from the European Nucleotide Archive under accession PRJEB107991. The DADA2-formatted SILVA 138.2 taxonomic training set is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14169026 . The independent ASV analyses complement, but do not reproduce or replace, the proprietary MicrobAT® workflow used for the primary OTU-based analysis. MicrobAT® algorithms, OTU-assignment parameters, and the release of its embedded reference database were not disclosed by the software provider. Accordingly, this archive supports reproducibility of the independent R1/R2 ASV sensitivity analyses and downstream analyses of the published MicrobAT® outputs, but not reconstruction of the proprietary MicrobAT®-generated OTU and taxonomic profiles. This version supersedes the earlier R-only archive by adding the Python utilities, complete operational documentation, software-environment records, random seeds, integrity checks, and portable figure-generation scripts.

summary: Our earlier note (rejected from an SC26 AI4S workshop, subsequently published as AIIT Bulletin Vol. 20) compared classical reduced-order models (POD, DMD) against naive neural surrogates (a fully-connected network, a CNN) on textbook-scale problems (lid-driven cavity, dam-break), on a single consumer GPU workstation. That note left five concrete gaps: no graph-based neural baseline, no industrially complex geometry, weak statistical evidence (nine snapshots, a single seed), no learned-dynamics counterpart to DMD, and no hyperparameter search for the neural baselines. This paper closes four of those five. The test case is an industrially representative two-phase stirred tank — a six-blade rotating impeller on a sliding (AMI) mesh, a bottom sparger injecting gas into water, ∼167k cells, solved with OpenFOAM's twoPhaseEulerFoam — run entirely on a single Mac Studio (Apple M4 Max, 14 cores, no discrete GPU). We benchmark five methods (POD, DMD, a neural network, a Graph Neural Operator, and a Deep Koopman autoencoder) on a genuine extrapolation task, backed by a 400-run statistical-robustness sweep, hyperparameter searches for both neural baselines, a check across three impeller speeds, and a four-level forcing-irregularity sweep (quasi-periodic through chaotic, direction-reversing impeller motion) intended to locate DMD's failure point. DMD wins consistently across every data scale, truncation choice, operating condition, and forcing-irregularity level tested, at both a 1 s and an extended 3 s prediction horizon – we did not find the failure threshold we went looking for, and report that directly. The search was not wasted, however: a Deep Koopman autoencoder, competitive at 1 s, degrades sharply at 3 s from compounding autoregressive rollout error (exposure bias); two independent, cheap mitigations – a physical [0, 1] clip mirroring the Graph Neural Operator's own implicit stabilization, and multi-step scheduled-sampling training – each recover roughly a third to a half of the gap without closing it, confirming the diagnosis. A separate, unplanned check turns up a sharper result: ranking methods by mass conservation rather than per-cell accuracy reorders them completely, with the most accurate method (DMD) only third-best at holding a basic physical invariant. We treat all three investigations as concrete instances of a broader, practical question for this community: how much genuine, open-ended scientific investigation — not just a fixed benchmark — can a single high-end workstation support before an HPC allocation is actually necessary? All code, case files, and Colab notebooks are released on GitHub for reproduction.
title: How Far Does One Workstation Go? A Pre-HPC Efficiency Check for Industrial-Scale CFD and Reduced-Order Model Benchmarking

summary: FPGA-Accelerated Sub-Microsecond Union-Find Decoding for Real-Time Surface-Code Quantum Memory Architecture manuscript. Latency, power, and resource figures are design estimates unless otherwise marked as measured. Related FPGA Union-Find implementations (Helios / Collision Clustering) are cited for comparison. Abstract Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires continuous decoding of stabilizer syndromes within cycle times that, for superconducting processors, are often 200 ns–1 μs. Host-processor decoders are subject to operating-system jitter, DMA overhead, and memory-hierarchy latency, which make deterministic sub-microsecond service difficult. This paper describes a fully pipelined FPGA architecture for a Union-Find decoder aimed at surface-code quantum memory. The pipeline integrates Aurora-based syndrome acquisition, streaming defect extraction, a path-halving Union-Find engine with hazard forwarding, localized peeling, and dual-port Pauli-frame updates. All latency-critical state is on-chip (BRAM, UltraRAM, distributed RAM). At a target clock of 400 MHz the design estimate for end-to-end latency is 170–390 ns below threshold, with a conservative worst-case bound near 500 ns—inside a 1 μs cycle. Memory for a decoding window scales as O(d³) with the space-time graph, not as O(d³) measurements per cycle. Power is estimated at 3–6 W per logical patch at the FPGA, which remains at room temperature. The contribution is a single deterministic pipeline that does not require a host CPU in the inner loop. It is an architecture and resource plan; it does not replace measured implementations such as Helios. Keywords: surface code; quantum error correction; Union-Find decoder; FPGA; real-time decoding; Pauli frame; clock gating. 1. Introduction Surface-code fault tolerance proceeds by repeated stabilizer measurement and classical decoding of the syndrome stream [1], [9], [10]. Superconducting cycle times commonly fall in T_cycle ~ 200 ns–1 μs [13]. Software decoders on CPUs or GPUs introduce scheduling jitter, DMA cost, cache misses, and synchronization [14]–[16]. Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is accurate but worst-case cubic in the number of defects and heavy for large distance [17], [18]. The Union-Find decoder of Delfosse and Nickerson is almost-linear and close to MWPM in accuracy, which makes it a natural hardware target [3]. FPGA and ASIC decoders have already shown that real-time surface-code decoding is possible. Das et al. gave a Union-Find micro-architecture; Liyanage et al. (Helios) implemented distributed Union-Find on a VCU129 up to d = 21 with mean times of order 10 ns per round under phenomenological noise, and a resource-optimized d = 51 point near 544 ns per round [14], [15]. Collision Clustering, another Union-Find variant, has been mapped to FPGA and ASIC with sub-microsecond times at large patch size [16]. The present manuscript specifies a single-tile, fully streaming pipeline—acquisition through Pauli frame—with explicit memory equations, banked Find ports, path-halving (not recursive compression), clock-enable power control, and a latency budget written against T_cycle = 1 μs. It is intended as a self-contained hardware architecture that can be implemented or compared against those measured designs. 2. System Architecture The decoder is a fixed-depth pipeline. Stages are registered and advance on the same clock. After fill, a new syndrome frame can be accepted every cycle from the control layer; variable work inside Union-Find is bounded by a worst-case iteration budget, not by a host thread. Stages: •     Syndrome acquisition and deserialization (Aurora 64B/66B over GTY). •     Defect extraction unit (DEU): frame-to-frame XOR and sparse packing. •     Pipelined Union-Find engine: growth, union, path-halving find, boundary test. •     Localized peeling
title: FPGA-Accelerated Sub-Microsecond Union-Find Decoding for Real-Time Surface-Code Quantum Memory

summary: The RNA world hypothesis faces two core challenges: first, the error threshold paradox—the contradiction between the length required for RNA replication and its fidelity; second, the transition from free RNA to a primitive cell (membrane-encapsulated system)—how to spontaneously form a selectively permeable compartmental structure. Dual Information Cybernetics states that internal information (the intrinsic determinacy of a system) possesses four attributes: wholeness, potentiality, self-consistency, and dominance. Among these, dominance drives the system from disorder to order and delimits the boundary of possibility for all local processes. Based on this theory, this paper proposes two mutually supporting experimental protocols: (1) the RNA condensate experiment—under mild wet-dry cycling conditions, observing whether RNA with secondary structure spontaneously forms condensates and testing whether the replication fidelity within the condensate is higher than that of single molecules, thereby verifying that "collective synergy" can bypass the error threshold; (2) the RNA-lipid co-assembly experiment—under the same mild conditions, observing whether RNA actively attracts lipid molecules and drives vesicle formation, forming an RNA-containing protocell model, thereby verifying the "active nest-building" behavior driven by the dominance of internal information. Both experiments share the same theoretical framework and mild-condition design; their results corroborate each other and can provide direct visualizable evidence for the dominance of internal information. This paper describes in detail the experimental materials, apparatus, observational indicators, expected results, and significance, aiming to provide an actionable research protocol for experimental researchers and to advance the information-theoretic perspective on the origin of life.
title: Two Experimental Protocols for Verifying the Dominance of Internal Information in RNA From the Error Threshold to Protocell Construction

summary: Research data and software supporting the derivation and literature reconstruction of relative-sensitivity expressions in inverse multiple linear regression luminescence thermometry. Includes executable Excel calculations for 22 model-temperature cases from seven papers, literature classification and equation-lineage evidence, numerical reconstruction code, analytical figure data, editable figure sources, and preserved Lean 4 and AXLE verification records. Effective sensitivities are conditional on the stated reference noise model and recovered local gain. Unresolved reconstruction discrepancies and the limited scope of formal verification are documented.

summary: Full Changelog : https://github.com/attogram/fantastic-octo-giggle/compare/0001...0002 42 and the Open Error Foundation: An Academic Interpretation Abstract The relationship between 42 and the Open Error Foundation (i.o.) can be understood as more than a recurring joke, reference, or organizational number. It can function as a compact epistemological model for the Foundation itself. The central problem of 42 is not that the answer is numerically wrong. It is that an answer can be generated before the question has been adequately established. That distinction is extraordinarily relevant to an organization concerned with artificial intelligence, institutional systems, scientific error, education, and continuous experimentation. The Foundation's two central statements, "Error is the message" and "Sesame Street is the teacher," consequently form a complementary methodology. The first treats failure, contradiction, mismatch, and unexpected output as potentially informative evidence. The second establishes a method for responding to uncertainty: return to fundamentals, ask understandable questions, experiment, explain, repeat, and learn. 42 then represents the unresolved question at the center of the entire process. The organization does not claim to possess the ultimate answer. It asks whether we have actually identified the question. The 42 Problem: An Answer Without a Question The cultural origin of 42 is Douglas Adams' The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Within the story, the enormous computer Deep Thought spends millions of years calculating the answer to the "Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything." The result is: The fundamental joke is subsequently revealed: the beings who commissioned the computation do not actually know what the Ultimate Question is. A later computational project is therefore required to determine the question itself. This creates a particularly interesting epistemological structure: Question → computation → answer has been replaced by: computation → answer → realization that the question is unknown → search for the question That reversal is precisely what makes 42 relevant to AI. A modern AI system can produce an extraordinarily fluent answer to an inadequately specified question. It can produce something that looks like knowledge before the underlying problem has been properly framed. The resulting failure is therefore not necessarily: "The machine calculated incorrectly." It may instead be: "We never established what needed to be calculated." That is a much deeper category of error. Error Is the Message The Open Error Foundation's phrase "Error is the message" can therefore be interpreted as an epistemological proposition rather than simply a creative slogan. Ordinarily, error is treated as something to eliminate: correct → incorrect → remove incorrect But scholarship in the philosophy and history of science has explicitly examined the possibility that errors can have productive epistemic roles. Jutta Schickore's historical analysis argues that error can contribute to scientific practice rather than merely obstruct it. More recently, Douglas Allchin's Toward a Philosophy of Error in Science develops an explicit framework around "error analytics," including error types, error signatures, checkpoints, error probes, and negative knowledge. His argument is that scientific practice is not merely about accumulating confirmations; it also depends on systematically identifying and managing ways in which knowledge can fail. This provides a serious academic foundation for the Foundation's intuition. An error can contain information about: the assumptions behind a system the limits of a model the framing of a question the quality of available evidence hidden dependencies institutional incentives human misunderstanding the difference between intended and actual behavior In this interpretation: An error is an observation about a system. The Open Error Foundation can therefore be understood as prac

summary: Abstract Data marketplaces and collaborative analytics require a way to estimate the value of contributed records without exposing the records themselves. This paper presents HKD_FACTOR_50, a protocol architecture that com-bines task-specific marginal-contribution valuation, addi-tively homomorphic aggregation, policy-bound release, and an auditable payment ledger. The construction does not claim that encryption makes arbitrary machine-learning training private. Instead, it protects a deliber-ately restricted interface: contributors encrypt quantized valuation statistics, an evaluator computes approved linear aggregates on ciphertexts, and a threshold or designated decryptor releases only authorized totals. We define cor-rectness, confidentiality, integrity, and audit requirements; describe leakage and collusion boundaries; and provide a complete executable Python reference demonstration based on the Paillier cryptosystem. The program verifies encrypted weighted aggregation against plaintext compu-tation and rejects tampered ledger entries. The reference code is pedagogical rather than production-hardened, but it makes the protocol’s data flow and invariants repro-ducible. HKD_FACTOR_50 therefore supplies a concrete baseline for privacy-preserving data valuation while iden-tifying the additional controls required for deployment: authenticated transport, robust key custody, range proofs, differential-privacy release, and independently reviewed cryptographic libraries. Keywords Data valuation; homomorphic encryption; authenticate participants, and control what is released. privacy-preserving computation; Paillier cryptosystem; secure data sharing; auditability; data marketplace; Shapley value.
title: HKD_FACTOR_50: Secure Data Valuation and Sharing via Homomorphic Encryption

summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). Pre-release adversarial verification (four independent refuter passes) confirmed all headline statistics against the raw data and caught an inverted flagship anecdote: the corpus's two catastrophic degenerations (~50 verbatim paragraph repetitions) were selected once and avoided once by the governor, undetected in both cases — set-based trigram signals are structurally blind to within-output verbatim repetition. All tasks, rollouts, verdicts, audit votes, and analysis code are released in the companion repository. AI co-observer: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) — working method only; blind pairwise judging by Claude subagents under a position-swapped two-vote protocol; four independent adversarial refuter passes preceded release; the registered author is the human author alone. Version 1.1 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a proof-backed clarification that at window 3 the saturation condition is exactly “three identical consecutive non-rewrite change types” (the 0.70 threshold is inert there; companion note DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22842506), (ii) a pre-registered evaluation of a repetition-ratio guard as a fourth, roll-back signal — fires on both known collapses and 200/200 synthetic inflations, on 0 of 7,998 remaining published generations, 0 of 60 template expansions, and 0 of 960 held-out generations (verdict GO; pre-registration commit a89f722 precedes all evaluation data), and (iii) an expanded AI-authorship disclosure. All v1.0 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.2 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a length-stratified reanalysis of the 621 judged governor pairs (loss rate 92% where the early text is under 60% of the final length, 16.1% at near-equal length; 31 losses vs 4 wins at matched length, sign test p < 10 -5 — evidence of a content cost independent of length, not a decomposition of the headline cost), (ii) a held-out replication on 60 tasks authored after the fourth-signal pre-registration (token reduction 34.5% / 34.5%, loss rate 31.7% / 36.7%, main-study values inside the held-out intervals), and (iii) an online-intervention verification: an incremental governor reproduces all 1,000 published decisions (0 mismatches) and, run as a genuine online loop on the 60 held-out tasks with the 12B generator, generates 319 of 480 iterations with a stop distribution indistinguishable from the offline policy (permutation p = 0.46). All v1.0 and v1.1 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.3 (2026-09-19): adds a pre-registered length-matched re-judging (100 governor-loss pairs with early/final length ratio < 0.80; final text truncated at sentence boundaries to the early text's word count): the early text beats the length-matched final in 94/100 (loss 4%), and the full final beats its own truncation in 100/100. summary: Chinese-SkillSpan provides competency-span annotations for Chinese job advertisements, annotation guidelines, and evaluation tools. The original corpus contains 22,840 sentences from four recruitment collections. Version v0.1.3 includes a 150-sentence human reference and released Silver-plus B2 training and development files. The flat, ESCO-informed label inventory distinguishes language, knowledge, occupational skills, and transversal competences. Historical evaluation protocols and later expanded-Silver experiments are documented separately in the project repository.
title: Chinese-SkillSpan: A Benchmark for Competency Span Extraction from Chinese Job Advertisements

summary: This repository contains the official R implementation and replication scripts for the research paper: "Evaluating Feature Selection for Uncertainty Quantification in Digital Soil Mapping: A Case Study of Soil pH" . Overview Digital Soil Mapping (DSM) frameworks require robust feature selection (FS) to mitigate collinearity and enhance spatial prediction while properly characterizing predictive uncertainties. This study systematically evaluates six feature selection methods across five machine learning and quantile regression models for soil pH mapping. Workflow Components Feature Selection Methods (6): Variance Inflation Factor ( VIF ) Recursive Feature Elimination ( RFE ) Simulated Annealing variants ( SA-FS1 , SA-FS2 ) Genetic Algorithm variants ( GA-FS1 , GA-FS2 ) Machine Learning Algorithms (5): Support Vector Machine ( SVM ) Random Forest ( RF ) Cubist ( Cubist ) Extreme Gradient Boosting ( XGBoost ) Quantile Random Forest ( QRF ) Evaluation & Uncertainty Quantification (UQ): Scripts include parameter tuning, cross-validation workflows, point estimation metrics (RMSE, MAE, R²), and uncertainty quantification diagnostics (prediction interval coverage probability, interval width, and spatial uncertainty mapping). Repository Structure The scripts are structured into dedicated subfolders for each of the five models, providing standalone execution pipelines for feature selection, model fitting, and uncertainty estimation. Data Availability Due to institutional data-sharing policies and privacy considerations, the raw spatial and soil sample datasets are not hosted in this repository. Users can adapt the provided pipelines to their own raster covariates and soil point observation tables. Data access inquiries can be directed to the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Citation If you find this code useful in your research, please cite the corresponding publication (details provided in the README and publication metadata).
title: Feature Selection Framework for Uncertainty Quantification in Digital Soil Mapping

summary: We propose a synthetic-trained adaptive radial prediction filter for reversible quaternion graph lifting. Controlled synthetic regimes vary seven geometry factors; regime-optimal admissible filters are compressed into three prototypes. A seven-component decoder-visible descriptor drives a lightweight mixture estimator, with both bank and estimator trained entirely on synthetic data and frozen for target deployment. A parameter-free reference-routed update preserves exact reconstruction. On TotalCapture, the method reduces geodesic prediction MSE by   versus a nonadaptive cubic B-spline predictor that uses a single   radial filter across all neighborhoods, and   versus uniform Karcher averaging, without target-domain fitting or transmitted node-wise adaptation parameters.

summary: Raw and processed data, instrument configuration and analysis code from an experimental campaign on evaporation suppression by a modular floating cover, carried out between 14 August and 11 September 2026 at the Department of Nuclear Energy, Federal University of Pernambuco, Recife, Brazil (8.0476 S, 34.8769 W, 10 m a.s.l.). A Class A evaporation pan of 1.185 m internal diameter (1.1029 m2 free surface) was instrumented with a Campbell Scientific CR1000 datalogger recording at a 1 min interval: water level (QDY30A hydrostatic transducer), incident short-wave irradiance (Kipp & Zonen SP-LITE, with a LI-COR LI200X as secondary sensor), air temperature and relative humidity (Vaisala HMP45C), water temperature at three depths (Campbell 108 thermistors) and air velocity (Campbell 034A/034B). Radiative forcing was supplied by a dimmer-controlled array of 18 infrared drying lamps of 250 W, and advection by a fan discharging horizontally across the water surface. The floating cover consisted of rigid hexagonal plates of 110 mm side, deployed as 27 plates (77.0 % coverage) or 26 plates (74.1 % coverage), in two geometries. Fifteen experimental windows span three advective regimes (about 2 m/s, about 3.3 m/s and no forced air flow) and irradiance from 106 to 940 W/m2. On 10 September the sensors were repositioned and pH and conductivity probes added; records from that date describe a different instrument geometry and are excluded from every window. Twenty photographs of the apparatus are included, each described in a caption file. The deposit contains the unmodified TOA5 record, a consolidated 1 min series with vapour pressure deficit and latent heat flux added, a table of evaporation rates for each experimental window obtained by linear regression of water level against time, the Python script that reproduces both processed files from the raw record, the CRBasic measurement program and the sensor wiring documentation. The README describes every column, its unit, the -99.999 missing-data sentinel and the time bounds of each window, including the exclusion of the buoyancy transient that follows cover deployment. A separate folder holds five short commissioning exports from 12 and 13 August 2026, included as provenance for the acquisition system. They show that the hydrostatic level transducer entered the logger program at version v7 and that the air temperature and humidity probe began returning valid readings on 13 August. No result depends on them. Suppression is reported both as a raw ratio of rates and after normalising each rate by the mean vapour pressure deficit of its own window, because the two figures differ by up to 13.7 percentage points: covered and uncovered windows were run at different times of day and therefore under different atmospheric demand. The processing script reproduces both. These data support the manuscript "Vapour pressure deficit control reveals a stable suppression efficiency of modular hexagonal floating covers across advective regimes: a rate-based pan study for semiarid Brazil".
title: Evaporation suppression by modular hexagonal floating covers over an instrumented Class A pan (MAISSER-PE, Recife, Brazil, August 2026)

summary: Medicine-level dataset and complete R analysis code for the retrospective cohort study Authorised in Europe, Awaited in Bulgaria: A Time-to-Event Analysis of Where the 3.9-Year Delay to Oncology Medicine Reimbursement Accrues (Department of Social Medicine and Public Health, Medical University of Plovdiv, Bulgaria). See README.md and codebook.md.

summary: This is the reproducibility archive for the revised SCIPRA study. It provides: the reconstructed source corpus as a manifest (per-document title, year, publisher, URL, and SHA-256 of the source text), enabling independent re-fetch and hash verification without redistributing copyrighted text; the reconstructed stance and stakeholder annotations with a codebook; the leakage-safe TF-IDF/RBF-SVM classifier code with out-of-fold predictions and metrics; the Policy Convergence Index (PCI/RPCI) computation and scenario manifest; the Table-3 stakeholder-salience values (Power, Legitimacy, Urgency → Stakeholder Influence Coefficient) with a recompute utility; the criterion-detection-threshold output with a byte-identity verification utility; and the manuscript figures, including the recovered generator for the methodology figure. Reproducibility is documented per claim. Several components are reproducible from included code and inputs (corpus manifest, annotations, classifier, PCI/RPCI, Table-3 arithmetic, and the methodology figure). The criterion-detection-threshold result is provided as a preserved output with a verification utility. Certain post-audit diagnostics (structural non-degeneracy, component ablation, and semantic-specification sensitivity), the revised Monte Carlo statistics, and several figure renders are provided as preserved values and renders: the reported values and rendered outputs are included, but their original generators are not, so those specific items are not independently re-executable from this archive. Raw full text of copyrighted sources is not included. The complete per-claim reproducibility postures and limitations are documented in the archive README and codebook. This version corresponds to the revised study and is a new version of the existing SCIPRA concept record; the earlier submitted-version deposit is retained unchanged.
title: SCIPRA: Stakeholder-Centric Investment–Regulatory Policy Architecture

summary: Full Changelog : https://github.com/attogram/fantastic-octo-giggle/compare/0001...0002 42 and the Open Error Foundation: An Academic Interpretation Abstract The relationship between 42 and the Open Error Foundation (i.o.) can be understood as more than a recurring joke, reference, or organizational number. It can function as a compact epistemological model for the Foundation itself. The central problem of 42 is not that the answer is numerically wrong. It is that an answer can be generated before the question has been adequately established. That distinction is extraordinarily relevant to an organization concerned with artificial intelligence, institutional systems, scientific error, education, and continuous experimentation. The Foundation's two central statements, "Error is the message" and "Sesame Street is the teacher," consequently form a complementary methodology. The first treats failure, contradiction, mismatch, and unexpected output as potentially informative evidence. The second establishes a method for responding to uncertainty: return to fundamentals, ask understandable questions, experiment, explain, repeat, and learn. 42 then represents the unresolved question at the center of the entire process. The organization does not claim to possess the ultimate answer. It asks whether we have actually identified the question. The 42 Problem: An Answer Without a Question The cultural origin of 42 is Douglas Adams' The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Within the story, the enormous computer Deep Thought spends millions of years calculating the answer to the "Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything." The result is: The fundamental joke is subsequently revealed: the beings who commissioned the computation do not actually know what the Ultimate Question is. A later computational project is therefore required to determine the question itself. This creates a particularly interesting epistemological structure: Question → computation → answer has been replaced by: computation → answer → realization that the question is unknown → search for the question That reversal is precisely what makes 42 relevant to AI. A modern AI system can produce an extraordinarily fluent answer to an inadequately specified question. It can produce something that looks like knowledge before the underlying problem has been properly framed. The resulting failure is therefore not necessarily: "The machine calculated incorrectly." It may instead be: "We never established what needed to be calculated." That is a much deeper category of error. Error Is the Message The Open Error Foundation's phrase "Error is the message" can therefore be interpreted as an epistemological proposition rather than simply a creative slogan. Ordinarily, error is treated as something to eliminate: correct → incorrect → remove incorrect But scholarship in the philosophy and history of science has explicitly examined the possibility that errors can have productive epistemic roles. Jutta Schickore's historical analysis argues that error can contribute to scientific practice rather than merely obstruct it. More recently, Douglas Allchin's Toward a Philosophy of Error in Science develops an explicit framework around "error analytics," including error types, error signatures, checkpoints, error probes, and negative knowledge. His argument is that scientific practice is not merely about accumulating confirmations; it also depends on systematically identifying and managing ways in which knowledge can fail. This provides a serious academic foundation for the Foundation's intuition. An error can contain information about: the assumptions behind a system the limits of a model the framing of a question the quality of available evidence hidden dependencies institutional incentives human misunderstanding the difference between intended and actual behavior In this interpretation: An error is an observation about a system. summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). Pre-release adversarial verification (four independent refuter passes) confirmed all headline statistics against the raw data and caught an inverted flagship anecdote: the corpus's two catastrophic degenerations (~50 verbatim paragraph repetitions) were selected once and avoided once by the governor, undetected in both cases — set-based trigram signals are structurally blind to within-output verbatim repetition. All tasks, rollouts, verdicts, audit votes, and analysis code are released in the companion repository. AI co-observer: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) — working method only; blind pairwise judging by Claude subagents under a position-swapped two-vote protocol; four independent adversarial refuter passes preceded release; the registered author is the human author alone. Version 1.1 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a proof-backed clarification that at window 3 the saturation condition is exactly “three identical consecutive non-rewrite change types” (the 0.70 threshold is inert there; companion note DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22842506), (ii) a pre-registered evaluation of a repetition-ratio guard as a fourth, roll-back signal — fires on both known collapses and 200/200 synthetic inflations, on 0 of 7,998 remaining published generations, 0 of 60 template expansions, and 0 of 960 held-out generations (verdict GO; pre-registration commit a89f722 precedes all evaluation data), and (iii) an expanded AI-authorship disclosure. All v1.0 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.2 (2026-09-19): adds (i) a length-stratified reanalysis of the 621 judged governor pairs (loss rate 92% where the early text is under 60% of the final length, 16.1% at near-equal length; 31 losses vs 4 wins at matched length, sign test p < 10 -5 — evidence of a content cost independent of length, not a decomposition of the headline cost), (ii) a held-out replication on 60 tasks authored after the fourth-signal pre-registration (token reduction 34.5% / 34.5%, loss rate 31.7% / 36.7%, main-study values inside the held-out intervals), and (iii) an online-intervention verification: an incremental governor reproduces all 1,000 published decisions (0 mismatches) and, run as a genuine online loop on the 60 held-out tasks with the 12B generator, generates 319 of 480 iterations with a stop distribution indistinguishable from the offline policy (permutation p = 0.46). All v1.0 and v1.1 numbers are unchanged. Version 1.3 (2026-09-19): adds a pre-registered length-matched re-judging (100 governor-loss pairs with early/final length ratio < 0.80; final text truncated at sentence boundaries to the early text's word count): the early text beats the length-matched final in 94/100 (loss 4%), and the full final beats its own truncation in 100/100. Pre-registered label: the losses on this stratum are attributab

summary: Medicine-level dataset and complete R analysis code for the retrospective cohort study Authorised in Europe, Awaited in Bulgaria: A Time-to-Event Analysis of Where the 3.9-Year Delay to Oncology Medicine Reimbursement Accrues (Department of Social Medicine and Public Health, Medical University of Plovdiv, Bulgaria). The dataset links 294 centrally authorised oncology medicinal products from the European Medicines Agency's public medicine data (marketing authorisation date and status, ATC code, therapeutic area, marketing authorisation holder, and the new active substance, generic, biosimilar, orphan, conditional approval, accelerated assessment, PRIME and advanced therapy designations) to the Bulgarian reimbursement record of the National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products: the start and end dates and outcome of the published HTA procedure, and the first appearance of each product in 130 dated monthly snapshots of Annex 2 of the Positive Drug List (16 October 2015 to 2 July 2026), with the provenance of each date. The primary cohort of the article is the 189 medicines authorised from 16 October 2015. The unit of observation is the medicinal product; no personal data are involved. The code reproduces every estimate, table and figure of the article and its supplement: Kaplan-Meier cumulative probabilities of reimbursement, decomposition of the interval into company submission and HTA assessment phases, Cox models stratified by product type (with robust, new-active-substance-only and advanced-therapy-excluded sensitivity fits), competing-risk and alternative-endpoint sensitivity analyses. See README.md and codebook.md.
title: Time from EMA marketing authorisation to reimbursement in Bulgaria for 294 centrally authorised oncology medicines, 2005-2026: medicine-level dataset and analysis code

summary: The analytical dataset and full extraction provenance for a study of how the cross-validation splitting rule affects machine-learning performance reported on literature-compiled membrane data. 512 canonical CO2/N2 permeation measurements were read from 82 open-access studies published 2020-2026. Every value carries the page it was read from, a content hash, and the DOI of its source. An identical panel of models was evaluated under two splitting rules: cross-validation grouped by source study, and a random row split. Contents: dataset.csv, the analytical dataset of 512 rows; observations.csv, pre-canonicalisation observations; citation_table.csv, every value attributed to its source DOI; fulltext_decisions.csv, the screening ledger with a reason for every decision; human_decisions.csv, the researcher's corrections; source_repairs.json, the sentence from the source justifying each repair; adjudication.json, contradictions between sources and how each was resolved; expansion_protocol.json, the corpus expansion protocol recorded before the run; rights_ledger.csv, rights_decisions.csv and rights_manifest.json, the release decision recorded for each study and what was withheld. No source PDF, rendered page image, or figure reproduced from a source is included. Each study is identified by DOI so that it can be retrieved from its publisher under that publisher's terms. Fourteen studies released their extracted values but not the short sentences quoted as evidence, because their licence could not be established or is not a Creative Commons licence; those sentences are marked as withheld in the files and listed in rights_manifest.json. All 512 rows are present, so the deposit reproduces the analysis reported in the manuscript.

summary: Code, retained reference inputs and derived data for a computational feasibility study of HGD editing in alkaptonuria. The shared-screen comparison retains 70 fixed canonical prime configurations and adds 79 PE3 configurations; with the constant base arm, representation is 110 versus 188 variants. The 93 already-canonical pairs are preserved, so no-loss is structural under common screens. Includes sequence reconstruction, sensitivity analyses and separately recorded panel follow-up computations. No biological experiments or educational-outcome measurements have been performed. Core reproduction and optional dependency scope are documented in verification records. The Mathematics, Engineering, and Science Achievement (MESA) program and Emerging Technologies Institute (ETI) at Foothill College provided funding and support for this project. Original code is licensed under MIT. Original project data, figures and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their original terms; see the included license and redistribution notices.

summary: Medicine-level dataset and complete R analysis code for the retrospective cohort study Authorised in Europe, Awaited in Bulgaria: A Time-to-Event Analysis of Where the 3.9-Year Delay to Oncology Medicine Reimbursement Accrues (Department of Social Medicine and Public Health, Medical University of Plovdiv, Bulgaria). The dataset links 294 centrally authorised oncology medicinal products from the European Medicines Agency's public medicine data (marketing authorisation date and status, ATC code, therapeutic area, marketing authorisation holder, and the new active substance, generic, biosimilar, orphan, conditional approval, accelerated assessment, PRIME and advanced therapy designations) to the Bulgarian reimbursement record of the National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products: the start and end dates and outcome of the published HTA procedure, and the first appearance of each product in 130 dated monthly snapshots of Annex 2 of the Positive Drug List (16 October 2015 to 2 July 2026), with the provenance of each date. The primary cohort of the article is the 189 medicines authorised from 16 October 2015. The unit of observation is the medicinal product; no personal data are involved. The code reproduces every estimate, table and figure of the article and its supplement: Kaplan-Meier cumulative probabilities of reimbursement, decomposition of the interval into company submission and HTA assessment phases, Cox models stratified by product type (with robust, new-active-substance-only and advanced-therapy-excluded sensitivity fits), competing-risk and alternative-endpoint sensitivity analyses. See README.md and codebook.md.

summary: cybedtools provides a reproducible R pipeline for ingesting, semantically representing (via a two-tier JSON-LD schema), and querying (via SPARQL) eleven major cybersecurity-related competency and learning-standards frameworks: NICE, DCWF, SFIA, ENISA ECSF, Cyber.org K-12, CSTA K-12 CS, ACM/IEEE CSEC2017, DigComp 2.2, CyQUAL, CCSSF, and OTCCF. The cybed: vocabulary uses cybed:OrganizingUnit as the cross-framework abstract for parent units and cybed:Role as a workforce-restricted subtype, with cybed:Subpoint and cybed:Example separating framework-as-specified enumerations from pedagogical-scaffolding examples. Includes a six-layer data-integrity verification rig and per-framework provenance manifests.

summary: State observation over the Hamilton division algebra is formulated as a structured realization problem for quaternionic multi-input multi-output systems. A left-intertwiner equation unifies companion assignment, row-oriented robust pole assignment, and coupled target realization with explicit noncommutative product order. A unitary measured-subspace decomposition yields a derivative-free observer with n-r dynamic quaternion states, where r = rank C, and reduces observability and detectability to a smaller pair. This order is minimal within the stated quaternion-linear full-state observer class. For full-order observers, structured H2 Lyapunov equations and an exact fixed-target gradient allow noise attenuation without moving the spectrum. For minimum-order observers, the reconstruction exposes the direct noise term and its interaction with pole-invariant injection freedom. Discrete-time formulas include the finite contribution of direct feedthrough, and correlated redundant outputs are characterized as noise references. Reproducible studies verify the gradients, compare quaternion, structured-complex, and real representations, expose the noise-cost nonuniqueness of maximum-volume designs, and test coupled repeated-class targets and a multi-output minimum-order observer.
title: Full- and Minimum-Order Quaternionic MIMO Observers: Spectral Assignment and Noise Geometry

summary: This repository contains the data, documentation, and replication materials associated with the data paper on the  Cartulario de Santo Toribio de Liébana . It records corrections and normalization decisions while maintaining traceability to the underlying documentary act. The package is therefore intended not only to reproduce the published dataset but also to make individual coding decisions auditable. The dataset is designed for reuse in research on medieval economic history, property transactions, monastic institutions, historical geography, social networks, and computational approaches to diplomatic sources.

summary: Background: Dried Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula Retz.) fruit, Dried Amalaki ( Phyllanthus emblica L.) fruit, Dried Vidanga ( Embelia ribes Burm.f.) fruit, Dried Trivruta ( Operculina turpethum (L.) Silva Manso) root and Dried Haridra ( Curcuma longa L.) rhizome; These drugs require reliable diagnostic characteristics for authentication and quality control for use in treatment of Dadru (dermatophytosis) . This study comparatively evaluated their organoleptic, macroscopic, and powder-microscopic characteristics to identify key diagnostic features. Materials and Methods: Authenticated samples of Haritaki, Amalaki, Vidanga, Trivruta and Haridra were evaluated for their organoleptic, macroscopic and powder microscopic characteristics using standard pharmacognostical methods. Diagnostic features were documented by light microscopy and compared with pharmacopoeial references . Results: Pharmacognostical evaluation of Haritaki , Amalaki , Vidanga , Trivruta and Haridra confirmed their authenticity through organoleptic, macroscopic and powder microscopic examinations. Each drug exhibited distinct diagnostic features such as characteristic taste, odour, fracture, and microscopic markers including fibres, stone cells, starch grains, sclereids, vessels and oleoresin cells, consistent with pharmacopeial standards. Conclusion: The study established reproducible diagnostic parameters for the selected drugs, ensuring accurate identification and quality control. These findings provide baseline pharmacognostical data for quality assessment of the selected drugs intended for formulations used in Dadru (dermatophytosis).

summary: R code, input parameters and generated outputs reproducing every result of the accompanying article. The analysis is a decision-analytic state-transition (Markov) model comparing four strategies for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, aficamten, mavacamten, alcohol septal ablation and septal myectomy, in Germany and the United States, with standard medical therapy as a secondary reference arm. It covers the four-strategy efficiency frontier, four separately defined annual acquisition-price thresholds, probabilistic sensitivity analysis over 10 000 draws with common random numbers, and an age-specific specification for starting ages 40 to 85 years using national life tables and published age-stratified procedural risks. Contents: 16 R scripts, two life-table input files, and 70 generated outputs (tables, figures and logs). Running "Rscript run_all.R" from a clean directory regenerates all of them. The run begins with an audit gate of 252 automated checks covering arithmetic identities, the provenance of every price, the separation of the four price concepts, the wording of categorical results, and the internal consistency of the cross-trial declaration. No output is written unless every check passes. No individual patient data are included or required. All inputs are published trial results, national tariff catalogues, national life tables and explicitly declared assumptions; each is listed with its source, or with the explicit absence of one, in the provenance register. Requires R 4.6.0 or later with ggplot2, dplyr, scales, patchwork, ggrepel and jsonlite.
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Myosin Inhibitors and Septal Reduction Therapies for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

summary: Derived tables and provenance registries supporting source-resolved mass absorption efficiency (MAE) estimates for wintertime brown carbon from residential solid-fuel and fossil-fuel combustion across European and Chinese sites. Contents: (i) source-resolved MAE estimates for the European station pairs and six Chinese cities with block-bootstrap percentile intervals and trustworthiness grading; (ii) station metadata and the field-level verification status of the Chinese records; (iii) per-dataset variable-group coverage tables and sensitivity analyses; (iv) the 84-field variable dictionary of the harmonized master table; (v) per-dataset provenance registries recording authoritative archives, citations and access routes, including a per-file DOI registry for the EBAS absorption compilation; (vi) the evidence tables underlying the Supporting Information (spectral benchmarks, coverage analyses, validation tables, perturbation domains, and the literature-coordinate conversion audit); (vii) an integrity baseline of file checksums for independent verification. Primary hourly records are not redistributed and are available from the original archives identified in the provenance registry or from the authors on request. The harmonized master table itself is not included. Earlier versions and superseded analyses are documented in the version history; the current release is the curated final set. v1.7.0 (2026-09-20) : third-round revision-companion update. Adds the pricing estimand registry (coal: Kraków 2018/19 pure-CCOA median 4.61 m² g⁻¹; biofuel: five-station winter-matched effective 3.84 m² g⁻¹), the source-omission benchmark with locked-λ bootstrap loss distributions, placebo arms and model-available bulk predictors, the unified canonical interval products and block-length sensitivities, the canonical-construction coverage harness, the conditional-ratio bootstrap draws, the locked SI table mirrors (SI_Table_S26–S31.csv), and the figure-generation and 370 nm conversion scripts. See README_v1.7.0_addendum.md inside the archive for the file-level inventory.

Contents: (i) source-resolved MAE estimates for the European station pairs and six Chinese cities with block-bootstrap percentile intervals and trustworthiness grading; (ii) station metadata and the field-level verification status of the Chinese records; (iii) per-dataset variable-group coverage tables and sensitivity analyses; (iv) the 84-field variable dictionary of the harmonized master table; (v) per-dataset provenance registries recording authoritative archives, citations and access routes, including a per-file DOI registry for the EBAS absorption compilation; (vi) the evidence tables underlying the Supporting Information (spectral benchmarks, coverage analyses, validation tables, perturbation domains, and the literature-coordinate conversion audit); (vii) an integrity baseline of file checksums for independent verification. Primary hourly records are not redistributed and are available from the original archives identified in the provenance registry or from the authors on request. The harmonized master table itself is not included. Earlier versions and superseded analyses are documented in the version history; the current release is the curated final set. v1.7.0 (2026-09-20) : third-round revision-companion update. Adds the pricing estimand registry (coal: Kraków 2018/19 pure-CCOA median 4.61 m² g⁻¹; biofuel: five-station winter-matched effective 3.84 m² g⁻¹), the source-omission benchmark with locked-λ bootstrap loss distributions, placebo arms and model-available bulk predictors, the unified canonical interval products and block-length sensitivities, the canonical-construction coverage harness, the conditional-ratio bootstrap draws, the locked SI table mirrors (SI_Table_S26–S31.csv), and the figure-generation and 370 nm conversion scripts. See README_v1.7.0_addendum.md inside the archive for the file-level inventory.
title: Source-resolved brown carbon MAE estimates: derived tables, variable dictionary, and provenance registries

summary: This manuscript identifies six substrates — individual memory, species lineages, externalised records, immune memory, the first generation of stars, and prion populations — which share a four-part mechanical structure, and among which no pair, to our knowledge, cites another. We specify the four mechanisms as an explicit screen, and validate it by applying it to cases that should fail: thermal equilibrium scores zero of four, sheared amorphous matter scores an intermediate two and a half, and stem cells score three of four in a manner that identifies precisely which mechanism is missing. We then derive, from this framework’s own commitment that any render of a record is necessarily partial, a scaling law governing all six: the more degraded the record, the more the reconstruction is determined by the template rather than by the record. We show this law is independently confirmed in four of the six fields, under four different names, by researchers not addressing one another. We supply a birth term that a companion manuscript’s earlier treatment lacked, deriving it from Bennett’s history-tape result rather than from biology, and show that a standard macroevolutionary survivorship formula then applies to memory unchanged. Three results that did not hold are recorded in full, including one prediction that failed outright on simulation and one correspondence that was stated backwards relative to the data. The foundational architecture, geometric intuitions, and motivating philosophy of this framework originated independently with the author prior to and separate from any AI involvement. Subsequent mathematical derivation, connection to established physics literature, computational verification, and error-checking were conducted through extended technical work with AI systems (Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini). The author directed this process, evaluated and selected among proposed derivations, and takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the final work.

summary: Metrics Added MixtureMetric and MixtureComponent , which express a weighted linear combination of BaseMetric instances. This is exact, by linearity of expectation, and is how empcs_score now expresses a distribution that mixes a point mass with a continuous piece — something a single Metric cannot express, since SymPy cannot symbolically integrate over such a distribution. Added BaseMetric , the abstraction every loss parameter throughout the package now accepts. Metric and MixtureMetric both implement it, so either can be passed interchangeably as a model's training objective. Added the LogCost strategy for building custom expected log cost (weighted cross-entropy) metrics. expected_log_cost_loss is now built from it. Metrics built with the Cost and Savings strategies now accept stochastic ( sympy.stats ) cost parameters, reducing them to their mean. Previously this raised NotImplementedError: Random variables are not supported for the savings metric. at Metric construction time. Added constrain and constrain , which declare the values a cost-matrix parameter is allowed to take. A parameter can be given inclusive lower / upper bounds, or a callable can express a condition spanning several parameters at once ( constrain(lambda p: p['clv'] > p['incentive_cost'], message=...) ). Added Profit , MinCost and EmpiricalMinCost , the sign-flipped siblings of Cost , MaxProfit and EmpiricalMaxProfit . Each computes the same quantity as its partner and reports it with the opposite sign, so a cost matrix can be read as costs to minimize or as profits to maximize. The choice is presentational: the optimal threshold and rate are unchanged, and models fit identically on either member of a pair. Added EmpiricalMaxProfit and AUEPC strategies for building custom metrics that compute the empirical (convex-hull-based) maximum profit and the area under the empirical profit curve, respectively. Metric now warns ( UserWarning ) at construction when the cost matrix has no terms, or its terms cancel to exactly zero — such a metric always evaluates to 0.0 regardless of its parameters. Metric now warns when called with a parameter its cost matrix does not use, instead of silently ignoring it — catching a typo'd keyword argument. sample_weight and strategy-specific extras (e.g. Savings ' baseline ) are exempt. Multi-letter symbols now render upright in the LaTeX representations of CostMatrix and Metric , so a product such as clv * r reads as two variables rather than as one named clvr . Greek names such as gamma are unaffected. MaxProfit with integration_method='auto' now uses quasi-Monte Carlo for any number of stochastic variables whose distributions can be sampled, rather than only above two. Two stochastic variables used to go to nested quadrature. Pass random_state for a result reproducible across Metric instances; repeated calls on one instance were already identical. Deterministic MaxProfit metrics (a profit function polynomial in the stochastic variable) no longer compute the ROC convex hull, and evaluate the profit function vectorized over all operating points instead of in a Python loop. Quasi-Monte Carlo integration now covers eleven more distributions: BoundedPareto , Dagum , ExponentialPower (not published in SymPy's own documentation, so no link is possible), Frechet , Gompertz , LogLogistic , RaisedCosine , Rayleigh , Reciprocal , Weibull and WignerSemicircle . These previously fell through to plain Monte Carlo, which is around a thousand times less accurate for the same sampling budget. optimal_rate and optimal_threshold now always compute the exact EMP when one stochastic variable is present. MaxProfit accepts profit functions of any shape in the stochastic variable. Previously a cost matrix using exp , log or a square root raised PolynomialError from inside SymPy when the Metric was constructed. check_input has been removed from every prebuilt metric that is now a Metric / MixtureMetric instance ( empc_score , mpc_score , empb_score

summary: Hashing Is Not Retrieval is a prospectively frozen three-arm evaluation of context accumulation in small-model multi-agent code cartography. It compares three ways for an orchestrator to hand work to a worker: 1. FULL HISTORY — retransmit prior worker outputs. 2. OPAQUE REF — replace the previous output with an unretrievable SHA-256 digest. 3. RETRIEVED — resolve the digest through a tenant-scoped content-addressed store and inject the recovered bytes. All arms receive identical source-derived evidence. The apparatus measures the exact message content sent to workers and records token counts, model and provider identifiers, generation IDs, usage, cost, retries, and retrieval proofs. A five-task gate preceded a fixed 50-task controlled benchmark, followed by a separate state-required evaluation across 24 deterministic fixtures and a five-scale Medusa case study. Key result: in the controlled benchmark, RETRIEVED reduced paired peak context by 38.3% relative to FULL HISTORY. The state-required follow-up shows that opaque references fail when state must be recovered, while verified retrieval preserves substantially more structural information. This is bounded-context evidence for automatic orchestrator-resolved state passing inside a specific two-worker code-cartography harness — not a universal claim about autonomous memory, long-context capability, or reasoning quality. The release includes the corrected author-identified preprint, executable apparatus, frozen results, task fixtures, telemetry, and verification instructions. Version 1.0.2 supplies the curated, verifier-passing reproducibility archive. It supersedes the uncurated archive from version 1.0.1 and includes the exact pinned apparatus, state-required fixtures, frozen results, and archive verifier. Submission status: This preprint was submitted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Long Context Foundation Models (LCFM). summary: Code, result tables, and figures for a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study in which instruments for coronary artery disease (CAD) were filtered by colocalization (coloc.abf, PPH4 ≥ 0.8) with brain cell-type-specific cis-eQTLs from single-nucleus transcriptomics of human cortex (Bryois et al., Nature Genetics 2022). Of 274 CAD lead loci, 32 colocalized with brain-cell eQTLs, yielding 32 cell-annotated instruments (excitatory neurons 12, pericytes 7 after palindrome exclusion, oligodendrocytes 5, astrocytes 3, microglia 2, inhibitory neurons 1, OPC 1) explaining 3.4–5.6% of CAD liability on the liability scale. Random-effects inverse-variance weighted estimates (with weighted median, MR-Egger, leave-one-out, Cochran's Q and I², MR-PRESSO-analog global permutation, outlier correction, and MR-Steiger sensitivity analyses) are provided for ischemic stroke (OR 1.335, 95% CI 1.189–1.498, p = 1.0e-6), any stroke (OR 1.309, p = 8.5e-7), Alzheimer's disease (proxy-inclusive, and a clinically diagnosed replication arm), and major depression (null negative control). Cell-type-stratified analyses attribute the stroke effect to neuronal and neurovascular-unit (pericyte) expression programs. Contents: full analysis pipeline (R 4.6 / Python 3.13), all derived result tables (instruments, colocalization posteriors, harmonized exposure–outcome pairs, primary and stratified MR, leave-one-out, Steiger), publication figures (SVG/PDF vector plus ≥300 dpi PNG), the manuscript (v1.7), supplementary tables S1–S8, and the completed STROBE-MR checklist. Raw GWAS summary statistics are not redistributed; all sources are public (GWAS Catalog accessions GCST90132315, GCST006908, GCST006906, GCST90027158, GCST007511, GCST005839; eQTL record 10.5281/zenodo.7276971) and every number needed to reproduce the tables and figures is included.

summary: The analytical dataset and full extraction provenance for a study of how the cross-validation splitting rule affects machine-learning performance reported on literature-compiled membrane data. 512 canonical CO2/N2 permeation measurements were read from 82 open-access studies published 2020-2026. Every value carries the page it was read from, a content hash, and the DOI of its source. An identical panel of models was evaluated under two splitting rules: cross-validation grouped by source study, and a random row split. Contents: dataset.csv, the analytical dataset of 512 rows; observations.csv, pre-canonicalisation observations; citation_table.csv, every value attributed to its source DOI; fulltext_decisions.csv, the screening ledger with a reason for every decision; human_decisions.csv, the researcher's corrections; source_repairs.json, the sentence from the source justifying each repair; adjudication.json, contradictions between sources and how each was resolved; expansion_protocol.json, the corpus expansion protocol recorded before the run; rights_ledger.csv, rights_decisions.csv and rights_manifest.json, the release decision recorded for each study and what was withheld. No source PDF, rendered page image, or figure reproduced from a source is included. Each study is identified by DOI so that it can be retrieved from its publisher under that publisher's terms. Fourteen studies released their extracted values but not the short sentences quoted as evidence, because their licence could not be established or is not a Creative Commons licence; those sentences are marked as withheld in the files and listed in rights_manifest.json. All 512 rows are present, so the deposit reproduces the analysis reported in the manuscript. Version 1.0.1 adds the logged random audit: audit_draw.json (the sample, recorded before any row was inspected, with its seed), audit_log.jsonl (one verdict per row, each carrying the time it was given and the row's content hash) and audit_result.json (agreement and the error-rate bound). A random audit of 40 of the 512 accepted rows found 0 disagreements with the source page, bounding the error rate above by 7.2% (95% Clopper-Pearson). No data file changed between 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.

summary: FlowMLLab v1.8.4 is the review follow-up release of the complete 43-notebook, 26-lecture CFD-to-scientific-machine-learning course. summary: Within the Complementarity-First and Reciprocal Internal Complementarity research program, we study the linear perturbations of the smooth massive magnetic core constructed in the companion paper. The host is a supplied flat-space SU(2) Yang–Mills theory with one adjoint scalar, unit magnetic degree, and equal scalar and vector masses. The action and physical scales are not derived from reciprocity. Starting from the full Cartesian second variation and linear Gauss constraint, we organize the physical angular sectors without excluding translations, boundary phase, or neutral radiation. A positive whole-half-line comparison gives a 4/25 lower bound in the two-profile magnetic radial sector. The separate spherical electric-flux operator has a positive but unquantified gap after charge and boundary data are separated. Explicit first-nonradial matrices, a compact-annulus Schur reduction, symbolic-angular-momentum higher matrices, and rational core certificates give all-angular nonnegativity conditional on the stated background and sufficient certificate predicates. The framed kernel consists of three translations and one phase tangent. In a covariant derivative-and-mass completion, a compact-remainder argument gives coercivity modulo this collective space with an unquantified positive constant. The kinetic wave operator nevertheless has essential spectrum [0,∞): exactly Gauss-dressed photon packets retain the zero threshold. An exact translation–photon overlap constructs fields orthogonal to the full kernel in L2 whose energy tends to zero while their local core tends to a nonzero translation. Thus energy-space or local-moment projection, not ordinary L2 orthogonality, is required for the stated coercivity. The result is a conditional linear sign, kernel, and norm-control theorem, not nonlinear orbital stability, decay, a numerical mode spectrum, or a monopole population prediction.

summary: Archived reproducibility bundle for CellFate-Rx Generation 1: a preregistered reanalysis of the six-condition clonal-tracing dataset GEO GSE279162 (generated and deposited by Schaff et al., doi:10.1016/j.xgen.2026.101191). summary: Topic models, in particular Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), have been adapted to hyperspectral imagery (HSI) as a route to interpretable spectral mixtures: each spectral unit (canonically a pixel) becomes a document of quantised band-frequency tokens and the inferred topic-word distributions act as non-negative basis spectra. Yet the dominant evaluation criterion remains downstream classification accuracy, an accuracy-only view that is silent on whether the basis is reproducible, band-robust, calibrated, or actually outperforms standard linear baselines. We propose and instantiate a twelve-axis evaluation framework for LDA-style topic models on HSI that quantifies, on the same set of benchmarks: (F-1) classification macro-F1 compared across five method families (paired differences and a hierarchical Bayesian model), (F-2) topic-word coherence (c_v, c_NPMI, U-Mass), (F-3) seed stability for both LDA and two neural variants (ProdLDA, ETM), (F-4) capacity sensitivity across K in {4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16}, (F-5) band-mask robustness, (F-6) cross-method clustering agreement (LDA vs Felzenszwalb, SLIC, patches, pixels), (F-7) topic-label coupling via P(L | t) entropy and KL, (F-8) per-topic Hungarian-aligned identity tracking, (F-9) HIDSAG cross-preprocessing stability, (F-10) cross-scene topic transfer, (F-11) rate-distortion of the topic representation, and (F-12) external alignment of the topics with a spectral library and a method-rank cross-comparison. We apply the framework to six standard HSI benchmarks (Indian Pines, Salinas, Salinas-A, Pavia University, Kennedy Space Center, Botswana) and five subsets of the HIDSAG mineralogical database (GEOMET, MINERAL1, MINERAL2, GEOCHEM, PORPHYRY). The framework yields three findings that the accuracy-only view does not surface. First, on the labelled scenes the topic-routed soft classifier, which routes the raw spectrum to per-topic logistic experts, matches the raw-spectrum logistic baseline in macro-F1 (0.915 against 0.910, a paired difference of 0.005), while a logistic regression on the topic proportions theta alone trails the baseline by 0.325: the topics add an interpretable routing to the raw spectrum but do not replace it. Second, on Salinas-A under the SWIR-only band mask the paired ARI between canonical and masked dominant-topic maps reaches 0.766, while on Kennedy Space Center under every mask, and on Botswana under the SWIR mask, the same paired ARI collapses to approximately 0.01, separating scenes on which an interpretability claim is band-robust from scenes on which it is not. Third, the theta-only deficit holds on HIDSAG: over its nineteen mineralogical targets the topic-logistic classifier trails raw-logistic by 0.268 macro-F1 (lower on 18 of 19 targets), contrary to the prima-facie expectation that mineralogical mixtures favour topic decomposition over the raw spectrum. We release 3895 deterministic derived artefacts (449 MB), the builder source, the FastAPI backend, the React frontend, and a 109-endpoint test harness as a public, MIT-licensed reproducibility package.
