We propose and instantiate a twelve-axis evaluation framework for LDA-style topic models on HSI that quantifies, on the same set of benchmarks: (F-1) classification macro-F1 compared across five method families (paired differences and a hierarchical Bayesian model), (F-2) topic-word coherence (c_v, c_NPMI, U-Mass), (F-3) seed stability for both LDA and two neural variants (ProdLDA, ETM), (F-4) capacity sensitivity across K in {4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16}, (F-5) band-mask robustness, (F-6) cross-method clustering agreement (LDA vs Felzenszwalb, SLIC, patches, pixels), (F-7) topic-label coupling via P(L | t) entropy and KL, (F-8) per-topic Hungarian-aligned identity tracking, (F-9) HIDSAG cross-preprocessing stability, (F-10) cross-scene topic transfer, (F-11) rate-distortion of the topic representation, and (F-12) external alignment of the topics with a spectral library and a method-rank cross-comparison. We apply the framework to six standard HSI benchmarks (Indian Pines, Salinas, Salinas-A, Pavia University, Kennedy Space Center, Botswana) and five subsets of the HIDSAG mineralogical database (GEOMET, MINERAL1, MINERAL2, GEOCHEM, PORPHYRY). The framework yields three findings that the accuracy-only view does not surface. First, on the labelled scenes the topic-routed soft classifier, which routes the raw spectrum to per-topic logistic experts, matches the raw-spectrum logistic baseline in macro-F1 (0.915 against 0.910, a paired difference of 0.005), while a logistic regression on the topic proportions theta alone trails the baseline by 0.325: the topics add an interpretable routing to the raw spectrum but do not replace it. Second, on Salinas-A under the SWIR-only band mask the paired ARI between canonical and masked dominant-topic maps reaches 0.766, while on Kennedy Space Center under every mask, and on Botswana under the SWIR mask, the same paired ARI collapses to approximately 0.01, separating scenes on which an interpretability claim is band-robust from scenes on which it is not. Third, the theta-only deficit holds on HIDSAG: over its nineteen mineralogical targets the topic-logistic classifier trails raw-logistic by 0.268 macro-F1 (lower on 18 of 19 targets), contrary to the prima-facie expectation that mineralogical mixtures favour topic decomposition over the raw spectrum. We release 3895 deterministic derived artefacts (449 MB), the builder source, the FastAPI backend, the React frontend, and a 109-endpoint test harness as a public, MIT-licensed reproducibility package. Code and derived artefacts: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_LDA_HSI . Interactive web application: https://lda-hsi.fasl-work.com . Manuscript sources: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_LDA_HSI_Paper . summary: The COVID-19 pandemic altered human mobility and natural-resource management, potentially affecting wildlife in rural landscapes where conservation and livestock production coexist. This work evaluated temporal variation in mammal detections in the Bienes Comunales Santa Cruz Nuevo Wildlife Management Unit, Puebla, Mexico, using camera-trap data from two pre-pandemic surveys (2018 and 2019) and a post-restriction survey (2022). Sampling comprised 39 station-years and 3,193.31 effective camera-days. The work compared encounter rates, station-level occurrence, and observed and estimated species richness among years, and also examined associations between wild mammals, domestic animals, human activity, altitude, and vegetation attributes. Species richness varied substantially among years: 14 species were recorded in 2018, nine in 2019, and 11 in 2022. Chao2 estimates and station-based rarefaction supported this interannual variability rather than a consistent directional change. Gray fox ( Urocyon cinereoargenteus ) detections declined significantly during the post-restriction survey relative to the pre-pandemic baseline (rate ratio = 0.280, 95% CI = 0.129–0.604, FDR-adjusted q = 0.025). Other species showed uncertain or non-estimable temporal effects because of sparse detections or complete zeros. Raccoon detections were negatively associated with altitude, whereas gray fox and coyote detections were associated with livestock occurrence. These findings demonstrate species-specific temporal responses and emphasize that nondetection or nonsignificant results do not necessarily indicate ecological stability. Although the observed changes coincided with the COVID-19 period, they cannot be attributed exclusively to pandemic restrictions because the year also represented climatic, ecological, and management variation.
title: Fauna–Vegetation correlations and relative abundance in a fragmented landscape of Southwest Mexico: Pre- and Post-COVID-19 analysis

Grounded in rigor meeting NASA fault-tolerance standards and Google high-performance software engineering specifications, the framework formalizes the OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) operational loop for arbitrary executable targets—spanning algorithmic functions, machine learning pipelines, and abstract syntax tree (AST) source code. summary: MATLAB implementation, per-item numeric results and figure code for the study "Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment". A four-agent evaluator running on a locally hosted Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct judge scores each prompt as an artifact before any response exists, then scores the resulting response twice on identical items: once against criteria extracted from that prompt, and once against a fixed rubric that never sees it. Verifiable constraints are checked with the IFEval reference implementation rather than model-generated labels. The whole pipeline runs on consumer CPU hardware with no external API calls. Contents: src/ the MATLAB agents and run scripts; scripts/ the IFEval verifier and the figure code; data/ a SHA-256 manifest of all 4,275 benchmark prompts and the filtered IFEval subset; results/ per-item results for the main run (n = 500) and the ablation (n = 120), the construct-validation output and the IFEval verification output. Corpus not redistributed. No prompt or response text from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat-1M is included; the LMSYS agreement prohibits transfer to third parties and WildChat-1M carries flow-down obligations under the AI2 ImpACT licence. Prompts appear only as SHA-256 hashes, so an independently rebuilt corpus can be verified as identical to the one used here. The IFEval subset is included in full under Apache-2.0.

summary: Extended reasoning can increase response time and computational cost without improving an answer. Models may revisit unproductive steps or build further reasoning on an earlier mistake. This study evaluates whether Jev, a probabilistic decision maker, can provide an inexpensive error signal to help decide when additional reasoning is needed. We compare Jev with GPT-5.6 Luna on generated ordering and logic-grid puzzles and on the official released ZebraLogic test set. The generated questions are four-choice items with one correct answer among four. The official test set is used open-ended: Luna produces the full grid, Jev checks it without the solution key, and Luna may revise once when Jev does not judge the answer consistent. On the generated multiple-choice problems, Jev is 5 to 60 percentage points more accurate than Luna with reasoning disabled, at lower measured API cost, and every observed top-choice disagreement identifies a Luna error. On a stratified sample of 200 official ZebraLogic puzzles, exact-grid accuracy rises from 41.0% with reasoning disabled to 90.5% with high-effort reasoning. A revision pass adds two points in both settings, but a revision-only control shows the gain comes from the extra attempt, not from Jev's information: on the answers Jev flags, a plain second look is at least as accurate as the Jev-informed revision (16 versus 13 correct without reasoning, and 70 versus 70 at high effort). Jev detects 93% of the weak reasoner's errors with 92% precision, but only 10% of its high-effort flags identify errors. These results motivate using Jev or similar decision models in a model harness: software that controls when to continue, reconsider, retrieve evidence, or allocate more reasoning. An early check could help avoid spending further computation on a mistaken line of reasoning. The experiments measure checking of final answers, however, and do not measure reductions in hallucination or repetitive reasoning inside a harness. On the official benchmark, extra reasoning accounts for most of the accuracy, and the checker's information does not improve on a second attempt. Larger studies with balanced answer positions, selective triggers, and step-level feedback are needed to test whether checking improves accuracy or reduces total cost.
title: Evaluating Jev for Cost-Effective Candidate Verification: An Exploratory Study

It supports governed binary, positive-duration, dynamic-pupillometry, SCR-responsivity, and trial-level multilevel mediation workflows with explicit readiness and provenance contracts, inspectable priors, predictive checks, restricted optional full-MCMC fitting, diagnostics, posterior estimands, sensitivity analysis, predictive validation, and conservative reporting.

summary: The complete evidentiary record behind a study of nine public support instruments for carbon capture in the United States and Canada, 2005 to 2026. It includes the instrument table; a census of twenty-eight capture projects; a provenance table of 131 entries giving the document, identifier, access date and clause relied upon for every fact, each with a basis code; a register of twenty-four scoped negatives recording what was searched, over what universe, and what document would overturn the finding; the money tables; comparator tables covering geothermal support and three jurisdictions that condition public money on delivered outcome; and a disclosure table recording what delivered tonnage each project publishes. The outcome coding materials are deposited in full, comprising the frozen instructions, the evidence pack issued to coders, the worked example, the blank sheet, both coders' completed returns and the calculator that produces the reliability figures. A fact-to-record audit traces every figure and quotation in the associated article to the row it came from. Deposited so that any claim in the article can be reproduced or contested.

summary: Certificate archive for "A computer-assisted lower bound for Landau's constant" (Frank Wikström, Lund University). This archive is the computer-assisted part of the proof of the lower bounds B_inf > 0.51 for the locally univalent Bloch constant and L > 0.51 for Landau's constant, improving the bound 1/2 + 2·10^-8 of Chen and Shiba (2004). The manuscript is distributed separately and is not part of the archive. The certified statement is that each of the 1179 boxes of a finite cover of the normalized logarithmic coefficient body admits a schlicht disc of radius greater than 0.51. The smallest certified radius over the cover is [0.5100305329006052049176652 ± 4.18e-26], obtained with Arb ball arithmetic at 80 decimal digits. Contents (3.2 GB, single top-level folder landau-certificate-051/): - the cover manifest landau-cover-split-051-caps.json: the binary tree with exact dyadic splits, contractions and LP caps with their dual vectors, the 776 sources with SHA-256 digests, and the exact shift of every leaf; - the 776 certificate sources: cut descriptors, radial grids, angular arcs, sparse non-negative dual multipliers and curvature duals; - the reference verification run: twelve shard logs with the enclosure of every leaf, their transcripts, and the aggregation output; - the snapshot of the checker that produced those logs, with a SHA-256 inventory and a provenance record binding the logs to the manifest and the checker; - rejection tests, the search scripts that built the manifest from the stored sources, a pinned environment (CPython 3.12, python-flint 0.9.0, numpy 2.5.1, scipy 1.18.0), and the expected output of every command. The checker reconstructs every inequality from the stored exact data and does not call a linear programming solver or trust any stored numerical value; the floating-point search that found the multipliers is included for reuse but is not part of the proof. README.md gives three commands: aggregate the archived shard logs (about half a minute), verify a single leaf (a few minutes), and rerun the complete verification (about two hours on twelve cores). Released under the MIT License. Version 1.0.0.

summary: This dataset provides a curated and reproducible compilation of data used to analyze long-term trends in external-cause mortality in Ecuador from 1990 through 2024. The primary data sources are official mortality statistics and population estimates and projections published by Ecuador’s National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos, INEC). The dataset includes annual mortality counts and population-based indicators for major external-cause categories, including land transport injuries, other transport accidents and accidental injuries, suicide, homicide, events of undetermined intent, and other external causes. Where available, the data are organized by calendar year, sex, age or age group, geographic unit, ICD classification, and cause of death. Population denominators, crude mortality rates, confidence intervals, absolute and relative changes, mortality composition measures, sex-specific rate ratios, and variables used in the statistical analyses are documented separately from the original source data. summary: This dataset provides source records, recalculated supplementary tables, and reduced principal component analyses for woody crown hydraulic networks (WCHNs) from Caatinga and Cerrado vegetation in Brazil. It accompanies a critical review of the WCHN framework but is documented so that the dataset can be understood and reused independently of that manuscript. The deposit contains 13 files: three source spreadsheets, six recalculated or additional supplementary tables, one analytical PCA workbook, two PCA figures, and a comprehensive README. The source spreadsheets comprise 14 individuals of Cenostigma pyramidale classified into three WCHN size classes; ten additional Caatinga species represented by one WCHN each; and 15 Cerrado species represented by five WCHNs per species, totaling 75 networks. These spreadsheets preserve the WCHN diagrams, decomposition and topology records, original equations, and property values used in the source study. The supplementary tables recalculate symmetry (SYM), complexity (COM), and vulnerability (VUL) using revised equations. Revised SYM is expressed as the inverse coefficient of variation of IN–FN topological distances, SYM = 1/CV = μ/σ. Revised COM is COM = ΣNO × CV, making explicit the identity COM × SYM = ΣNO. Revised VUL excludes the initial node from the attackable set while preserving it as the root of the network, giving an attackable set of ΣNO − 1 nodes. Results are provided for C. pyramidale size classes, Caatinga species, Cerrado species, and phenological groups, as well as a comparison between Caatinga and Cerrado vegetation. The deposit also includes recalculated PERMANOVAs for the deciduous, semideciduous, and evergreen Cerrado groups. For recalculated property blocks, the analyses use species means, Bray–Curtis distances, and an exact enumeration of all 252 possible allocations of five species to each of two groups. An additional reduced-set PERMANOVA excludes the algebraically dependent properties COM and SHA. The DE–EV contrast was consistently the strongest pairwise differentiation, although its significance after correction for multiple comparisons depended on the property set analyzed. Separate reduced PCAs were performed for Caatinga and Cerrado using NAV, revised VUL, LAT, BAS, and PTP, without prior transformation and based on correlation matrices. The Caatinga analysis contains 24 WCHNs representing 11 species; its first two axes explain 91.1% of the total variance. The primary Cerrado analysis contains 74 complete cases from 15 species and excludes one network with an undefined BAS value; its first two axes explain 89.0% of the variance. A sensitivity analysis retaining all 75 Cerrado WCHNs by substituting the column mean for the single undefined BAS value produced essentially the same ordination structure. In both vegetation types, PC1 contrasts vulnerability with navigability, basitony, and potential topological plasticity, whereas PC2 is dominated by laterality. These convergent ordination structures identify two complementary dimensions of WCHN organization but describe covariance rather than causal relationships. The recalculated tables and reduced PCAs assess the topological component of the WCHN framework. They do not directly measure crown hydraulic resistance, xylem P₅₀, hydraulic safety margins, or causal effects on attained tree height. The dataset therefore provides comparative topological evidence and tests the framework’s internal structure, rather than fully validating hydraulic function mechanistically. The original analyses and table numbering are reported in Prado and Trovão (2023), Ecological Modelling , 481, 110345, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2023.110345 . Related stochastic WCHN data and computational experiments are available separately at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21839645 .

summary: This dataset provides source records, recalculated supplementary tables, and reduced principal component analyses for woody crown hydraulic networks (WCHNs) from Caatinga and Cerrado vegetation in Brazil. It accompanies a critical review of the WCHN framework but is documented so that the dataset can be understood and reused independently of that manuscript. The deposit contains 13 files: three source spreadsheets, six recalculated or additional supplementary tables, one analytical PCA workbook, two PCA figures, and a comprehensive README. The source spreadsheets comprise 14 individuals of Cenostigma pyramidale classified into three WCHN size classes; ten additional Caatinga species represented by one WCHN each; and 15 Cerrado species represented by five WCHNs per species, totaling 75 networks. These spreadsheets preserve the WCHN diagrams, decomposition and topology records, original equations, and property values used in the source study. The supplementary tables recalculate symmetry (SYM), complexity (COM), and vulnerability (VUL) using revised equations. Revised SYM is expressed as the inverse coefficient of variation of IN–FN topological distances, SYM = 1/CV = μ/σ. Revised COM is COM = ΣNO × CV, making explicit the identity COM × SYM = ΣNO. Revised VUL excludes the initial node from the attackable set while preserving it as the root of the network, giving an attackable set of ΣNO − 1 nodes. summary: We are pleased to announce the release of ASPECT 3.1.0. ASPECT is the Advanced Solver for Planetary Evolution, Convection, and Tectonics. summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

summary: Derived tables and provenance registries supporting source-resolved mass absorption efficiency (MAE) estimates for wintertime brown carbon from residential solid-fuel and fossil-fuel combustion across European and Chinese sites. summary: The article “The Image of Istanbul in the Russian Émigré, Soviet, and Modern Russian-Language Literature” explores various facets of the city’s image through the lens of the short stories and essays of the first wave of Russian émigrés’ literature, Soviet literary work of the 1920s-1930s, and contemporary Russian-language Azerbaijani prose. Literary works by Nadezhda Teffi Istanbul and the Sun (1921) and Gaito Gazdanov A Weak Heart (1927) explored in the article, focus on the émigré experience representing two most common ways of depicting Istanbul among the Russian émigré writers. Teffi neither succumbs to Orientalist fantasy nor reduces the city to a refugee misery, she supports both notions and considers Istanbul to be the city of exiles’ humiliation and artistic transcendence, whereas Gazdanov interprets the first center of Russian emigration more clearly and tragically, depicting it as a symbol of life without any moral support. Soviet literature portrays Istanbul in an entirely different manner. During the 1920s-1930s, the description of the East was ideologically justified as it implicitly prepared the ground for developing the internationalist theme of “the friendship of peoples”. Sweet Salt of the Bosphorus (2008) by a contemporary Azerbaijani author Elchin Safarli who takes into account the artistic experience of Russian émigrés, creates a transcultural space that exhibits the following features of transliterary writing: the author’s specific bilingual linguistic consciousness, the reconstruction of an Azerbaijani worldview through the Russian language, an interlinguistic textual field, the foregrounding of the cultural integration of Russians in the East and an objective reconstruction by the writer, who belongs to the Eastern cultural code, of a “Russian” perspective on the world.

summary: Administrative registers of missing persons routinely produce three types of outcomes that conventional descriptive statistics treat as if they were one: cases with no outcome yet (genuine indeterminacy, characteristic of an ongoing search process), cases with an explicit negative outcome (for example, a report that was retracted or dismissed), and cases in which two extracts or two operational definitions of the same register yield incompatible figures. This article takes as its case study the missing-persons register of Ecuador's Ministry of the Interior, already documented and corrected in a previous round of factual auditing, and reframes it as a textbook example of what we call typed abstention: the formal distinction between "not on record" (no outcome has been recorded yet), "recorded as negative" (explicit denial), and "evidence conflict" (sources or definitions that do not match). Using the real, already-verified data - 4,892 records as of the August 19, 2026 extract, with 3,485 resolved cases (71.2%) and 1,407 under investigation (28.8%), against 4,507 records and the 742/3,528/237 breakdown (under investigation/located alive/deceased) of the July extract - we show that the 385-record discrepancy between extracts and the disparity among the 78.28%, 83.54%, and 71.2% resolution rates are not errors but instances of exactly the three types of indeterminacy that the evidential-reasoning literature (Dempster-Shafer theory, AGM belief revision, Belnap-Dunn four-valued logic) has been formalizing for decades with tools native to that tradition. We complement the analysis of the real data with an illustrative simulation study - explicitly synthetic, not derived from the real register - that quantifies, through 20,000 synthetic cases and 100 Monte Carlo replicates per scenario, how much of the aggregate gap between two extracts of the same register can be explained by asymmetric underreporting without any real contradiction between the sources, and how much information is lost when a binary "resolved/unresolved" scheme collapses genuine indeterminacy and negative closure into a single ambiguous category. The simulation results show that an underreporting asymmetry of just 10 to 20 percentage points between two extracts can produce aggregate gaps of 6.8 to 13.6 percentage points in the observed resolution rate - of the same order of magnitude as the real 12.3-percentage-point gap in the resolution rate between the July and August 2026 extracts - without either source being objectively wrong. We conclude that explicitly typing these three states, rather than collapsing them, improves the interpretability of public indicators without requiring complex inferential statistics or assumptions about the causes of the phenomenon.

summary: Administrative disability registries record certified cases, not disability as such: a person absent from the registry may lack certification because no certifiable impairment exists, because access to an evaluation board was unavailable, or because an evaluation is pending - three epistemically distinct situations that a single observed count cannot, by itself, distinguish. This paper reframes a nationwide descriptive analysis of Ecuador's National Disability Registry (Registro Nacional de Discapacidades, CONADIS/MSP; cut-off December 2023; N = 113,203 aggregated records representing 480,776 certified persons across 222 province-canton units) as an instance of typed abstention applied to administrative subregistration. We distinguish "not registered" (no consta: absence of a positive record, uninformative about the underlying condition) from a hypothetical "registered negative" (consta que no: an explicit denial after evaluation, a state that exists within the underlying certification process but is not exposed in the published open-data resource used here) and from internally conflicting evidence. Data quality auditing verified 100% structural completeness across all eight operational fields. The demographic and clinical profile shows a predominance of males (56.48%), adults aged 51 years and older (47.13%), physical disabilities (44.87%), and moderate impairment severity (45.78%). Guayaquil and Quito concentrate 30.83% of absolute registration volume, yet fall to the 134th and 144th of 221 population-normalized ranks, below the national median. Because the published registry cannot, by construction, separate certification capacity from underlying need, we add an illustrative synthetic simulation in which two data-generating mechanisms - pure certification-capacity heterogeneity and pure prevalence heterogeneity, each confounded with population size - produce observable correlations between the normalized rate and population that differ by only 0.021 (Pearson r = 0.949 vs. 0.928) despite sharing no causal mechanism, formalizing why the normalized rate cannot be read as need without an explicit, currently unavailable, capacity signal. We situate this identification problem within the literature on disability statistics (the Washington Group on Disability Statistics; the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health), administrative and missing-data quality, and evidential reasoning frameworks for typed indeterminacy (Dempster-Shafer belief functions, three- and four-valued logics, AGM belief revision), none of which have previously been applied to a cantonal-level disability registry of this kind.
title: Typed Abstention in Administrative Disability Registries: Certification Intensity, Subregistration, and the Limits of Cantonal Normalization in Ecuador's National Disability Registry (2023)

summary: This dataset supports the study “UDDPG-Net: Energy- and Fairness-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in Underwater Communication Networks.” It contains the simulation data, experimental results, and lake-based acoustic measurement records used for evaluating UDDPG-Net. The simulation data cover underwater acoustic propagation, mobility, interference, energy states, resource-allocation decisions, training configurations, benchmark comparisons with Random, Greedy, PPO, TD3, SAC, MADDPG, and DDPG-GA, as well as scalability, ablation, exploration, SHAP, computational-efficiency, and robustness analyses. The field-test component corresponds to six campaigns conducted in Fengquan Lake, Xinxiang, China, and includes environmental, motion, acoustic-channel, and packet-level variables such as water temperature, salinity, pH, conductivity, sound speed, ambient-noise PSD, link distance, subband SNR, propagation delay, Doppler shift, and packet reception ratio. Reconstructed raw-format field logs are additionally provided to reproduce the organization and statistical characteristics reported in the manuscript; these files are clearly identified as reconstructed records and should not be interpreted as original instrument acquisition files. README files and structured metadata are included to describe the variables, units, experimental conditions, and correspondence between the released data and the figures and tables in the paper.
title: UDDPG-Net: Energy- and Fairness-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in Underwater Communication Networks

The field-test component corresponds to six campaigns conducted in Fengquan Lake, Xinxiang, China, and includes environmental, motion, acoustic-channel, and packet-level variables such as water temperature, salinity, pH, conductivity, sound speed, ambient-noise PSD, link distance, subband SNR, propagation delay, Doppler shift, and packet reception ratio. Reconstructed raw-format field logs are additionally provided to reproduce the organization and statistical characteristics reported in the manuscript; these files are clearly identified as reconstructed records and should not be interpreted as original instrument acquisition files. README files and structured metadata are included to describe the variables, units, experimental conditions, and correspondence between the released data and the figures and tables in the paper.
title: UDDPG-Net: Energy- and Fairness-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in Underwater Communication Networks

summary: xinvert v0.3.0 Complete CUDA GPU back-end, a rename pass on the module and public API, and a thread-safe progress reporter. This release also folds in everything that had accumulated since v0.2.0 — v0.2.1 and v0.2.2 were developed but never published, so 0.3.0 is the next version on PyPI after 0.2.0. (Earlier gaps exist in this project too: 0.1.4–0.1.6 were tagged but never released.) Highlights GPU back-end for every equation type architect='gpu' now works for all seven solvers, not just the standard 2-D Poisson case: | equation type | CPU kernel | GPU kernel | | --- | --- | --- | | standard 1D | invert_standard_1D | invert_standard_1D_gpu | | standard 2D | invert_standard_2D | invert_standard_2D_gpu | | standard 2D full (flux form) | invert_standard_2D_full | invert_standard_2D_full_gpu | | standard 3D | invert_standard_3D | invert_standard_3D_gpu | | general 2D | invert_general_2D | invert_general_2D_gpu | | general 3D | invert_general_3D | invert_general_3D_gpu | | general 2D biharmonic | invert_general_bih_2D | invert_general_bih_2D_gpu | Red-Black SOR kernels with a shared loop skeleton ( _run_sor_2d_loop , _run_sor_3d_loop ), adaptive convergence-check intervals, and an optional per-call thread-block shape via iParams['gpu_block2d'] . GPU solves are bounded to one at a time ( gpus._GPU_MAX_CONCURRENT ) so dask can pipeline disk I/O against them, and CUDA context creation is done on the main thread. Measured on an RTX 3090: single timestep, 300 x 720: 17.3x (1.73 s GPU vs 29.99 s on one core) 12 timesteps, 300 x 720: ~1.6x over 12-core dask CPU (21.3 s vs 33.3 s) — at this size the solve is launch-bound, not execution-bound large grids, fixed 1000 iterations: up to 17.1x See the benchmark docs for the full sweep and the launch-overhead analysis. Module rename: numbas.py → cpus.py The CPU kernel module is now named for what it contains. xarray 's dask backend remains the multi-core path. API renames (breaking) Four public names lose a _test suffix that misdescribed them as test-only — they implement real discretizations used by shipped applications: | old | new | | --- | --- | | invert_standard_2D_test | invert_standard_2D_full | | inv_standard2D_test | inv_standard2D_full | | invert_GillMatsuno_test | invert_GillMatsunoFlux | | invert_Stommel_test | invert_StommelFlux | Users calling the old names must update; there are no aliases. The private __coeffs_*_test helpers became __coeffs_*Flux . Thread-safe live progress output printInfo output from dask worker threads and distributed clusters no longer interleaves. Each message is emitted as a single atomic write with the right parent header, so Jupyter and worker logs stay readable. Tests Seven CPU/GPU consistency suites ( tests/test_Gpu*.py plus tests/test_CpuGpuConsistency.py , ~1700 lines) asserting the analytic solution where one exists and CPU/GPU agreement otherwise; GPU cases skip cleanly when no CUDA device is present. Benchmark suite under tests/ , with machine-readable results in tests/results/*.json and figure regeneration via tests/plot_benchmarks.py . CI matrix: Python 3.9 – 3.12, 38 passed, 37 skipped . Housekeeping .gitattributes line-ending policy plus a one-off renormalization — the repository had a CRLF/LF mix that inflated diffs by thousands of lines. deriv() with the central scheme no longer converts numpy-backed input to dask; the rechunk is applied only to genuinely chunked data. Documentation: GPU status table, benchmark page and the parallel-inversions notebook brought in line with the implementation. Upgrade notes Breaking: the four API renames above. CUDA support is optional — import xinvert still works on machines without a GPU, and architect='cpu' remains the default. If you pin gpu_block2d , the default is still (16, 16) . Full diff: https://github.com/miniufo/xinvert/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0
title: xinvert: A Python package for inversion problems in geophysical fluid dynamics

title: xinvert: A Python package for inversion problems in geophysical fluid dynamics

summary: xinvert v0.3.0 Complete CUDA GPU back-end, a rename pass on the module and public API, and a thread-safe progress reporter. This release also folds in everything that had accumulated since v0.2.0 — v0.2.1 and v0.2.2 were developed but never published, so 0.3.0 is the next version on PyPI after 0.2.0. (Earlier gaps exist in this project too: 0.1.4–0.1.6 were tagged but never released.) Highlights GPU back-end for every equation type architect='gpu' now works for all seven solvers, not just the standard 2-D Poisson case: | equation type | CPU kernel | GPU kernel | | --- | --- | --- | | standard 1D | invert_standard_1D | invert_standard_1D_gpu | | standard 2D | invert_standard_2D | invert_standard_2D_gpu | | standard 2D full (flux form) | invert_standard_2D_full | invert_standard_2D_full_gpu | | standard 3D | invert_standard_3D | invert_standard_3D_gpu | | general 2D | invert_general_2D | invert_general_2D_gpu | | general 3D | invert_general_3D | invert_general_3D_gpu | | general 2D biharmonic | invert_general_bih_2D | invert_general_bih_2D_gpu | Red-Black SOR kernels with a shared loop skeleton ( _run_sor_2d_loop , _run_sor_3d_loop ), adaptive convergence-check intervals, and an optional per-call thread-block shape via iParams['gpu_block2d'] . GPU solves are bounded to one at a time ( gpus._GPU_MAX_CONCURRENT ) so dask can pipeline disk I/O against them, and CUDA context creation is done on the main thread. Measured on an RTX 3090: single timestep, 300 x 720: 17.3x (1.73 s GPU vs 29.99 s on one core) 12 timesteps, 300 x 720: ~1.6x over 12-core dask CPU (21.3 s vs 33.3 s) — at this size the solve is launch-bound, not execution-bound large grids, fixed 1000 iterations: up to 17.1x See the benchmark docs for the full sweep and the launch-overhead analysis. Module rename: numbas.py → cpus.py The CPU kernel module is now named for what it contains. xarray 's dask backend remains the multi-core path. API renames (breaking) Four public names lose a _test suffix that misdescribed them as test-only — they implement real discretizations used by shipped applications: | old | new | | --- | --- | | invert_standard_2D_test | invert_standard_2D_full | | inv_standard2D_test | inv_standard2D_full | | invert_GillMatsuno_test | invert_GillMatsunoFlux | | invert_Stommel_test | invert_StommelFlux | Users calling the old names must update; there are no aliases. The private __coeffs_*_test helpers became __coeffs_*Flux . Thread-safe live progress output printInfo output from dask worker threads and distributed clusters no longer interleaves. Each message is emitted as a single atomic write with the right parent header, so Jupyter and worker logs stay readable. Tests Seven CPU/GPU consistency suites ( tests/test_Gpu*.py plus tests/test_CpuGpuConsistency.py , ~1700 lines) asserting the analytic solution where one exists and CPU/GPU agreement otherwise; GPU cases skip cleanly when no CUDA device is present. Benchmark suite under tests/ , with machine-readable results in tests/results/*.json and figure regeneration via tests/plot_benchmarks.py . CI matrix: Python 3.9 – 3.12, 38 passed, 37 skipped . Housekeeping .gitattributes line-ending policy plus a one-off renormalization — the repository had a CRLF/LF mix that inflated diffs by thousands of lines. deriv() with the central scheme no longer converts numpy-backed input to dask; the rechunk is applied only to genuinely chunked data. Documentation: GPU status table, benchmark page and the parallel-inversions notebook brought in line with the implementation. Upgrade notes Breaking: the four API renames above. CUDA support is optional — import xinvert still works on machines without a GPU, and architect='cpu' remains the default. If you pin gpu_block2d , the default is still (16, 16) . summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study" . This package contains everything needed to regenerate every table, figure and reported number in the manuscript from the analysis outputs, except the raw trajectories. Systems and sampling: three FGFR1 kinase domain systems (wild type, V561M, N546K) in complex with erdafitinib, three independent 500 -ns replicates each , analysed over the 200 -500 ns plateau. Nominal sampling 4.5 us; realised aggregate production sampling 4.491 us. All three systems share a 9.28387 nm cubic SPC water box with 0.15 M NaCl (total atoms 78 , 608 / 78 , 609 / 78 , 624 ). Contents: - scripts/ - 14 analysis and plotting scripts (Python 3.10 ) covering every main and supplementary figure panel - tables/ - 38 per-replicate and summary result tables (CSV) - matrices/ - 24 DCCM matrices, common-subspace PCA projections and RMSD series (NumPy .npy) - mdp/ - GROMACS run-control files (minimisation, ions, NVT, NPT, production) plus the fully expanded grompp parameter file - tpr/ - the nine production run inputs (complete, with all parameters baked in ) - topology/ - GROMACS topology files ( system and protein topologies, posre.itp, ligand parameters, index files ) - README.md - directory layout, frame-selection rules, uncertainty conventions, table/figure provenance, and full run parameters Software: GROMACS 2024.6 (production) and 2024.3 (analysis), gmx_MMPBSA 1.6 .5 , MDTraj 1.10 .3 , Python 3.10 (NumPy 2.2 .6 , SciPy 1.15 .2 , Matplotlib). Frame selection: MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA energies were computed on frames extracted at 1-ns spacing ( 301 frames per intact replicate ; 291 for V561M replicate 2 ). Replicate-level statistics use one value per independent trajectory ( n = 3 per system ) and are reported as mean +/- SD ; frames within a trajectory are not treated as independent samples . Per-residue decomposition values are reported as mean +/- SEM , which can be converted to SD by multiplying by the square root of 3 . Important for regeneration: the production runs were executed as a 200 -ns run followed by a 300 -ns extension (gmx convert -tpr -extend). md.mdp therefore defines only the first 200 ns and must be read together with that extension step. See README.md section 7. Raw trajectories (approximately 13 GB, full atom resolution, 100 -ps output cadence) are available from the corresponding author on request .

summary: Code and data supporting the article "Capillary-driven networks obey Murray's law everywhere except at the meniscus". The archive contains three things. A self-contained MATLAB package that builds the figures of the article and recomputes every number quoted in its text, using a backtracking Newton iteration on a scale-invariant objective and requiring no toolboxes. A Python module that carries the same model on arbitrary graphs, including graphs with loops, where the flow is obtained from the nodal Laplacian rather than from the topology, together with a script that runs the verifications of Appendices C, F and H: the nine-channel graph with four independent loops, the envelope identity, the sweep over the driving degree, the three terminal conditions, the power-to-cost ratios and the Kamiya-Togawa law, and the case of several dissipation mechanisms in one channel. And a pixel-level digitisation of Fig. 7 of Zhang and Lorente, Sci. Rep. 13, 11278 (2023), against which Sec. V of the article is compared, with the source raster, the recovered coordinates in three formats, and an image comparing the reconstruction against the original. Neither optimiser uses the sizing law under test: each maximises the throughput at fixed cost from the resistance and the cost directly, so the residuals reported are an independent check of Eq. (7) rather than a restatement of it. The digitiser is deterministic and reproduces its 298 recovered points byte for byte. Code is released under the MIT licence (LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt). The source raster in data/ is reproduced unaltered from a CC BY 4.0 third-party article and remains copyright of its authors; see THIRD-PARTY.txt. README.txt describes the contents, how to run everything, and which printed quantities depend on the configuration block.

summary: This work studies whether internal rotation changes the longevity of source-free localized excitations in the reduced Enchan local time-rate field. The frozen scalar dynamics are S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with D = |grad S| and mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)); no continuing external torque, centrifugal force, primitive matter source, or added rotational potential is used during the reported evolutions. Stage A supplies the non-rotating source-free baseline. Stage B1 initializes rotating phase-space states at omega = 4, 8, and 12 and evolves the extended runs to dimensionless time t = 100. Over 80 <= t <= 100, the mean localized-energy fractions are approximately 0.002207 for the non-rotating baseline and 0.006006, 0.149470, and 0.368846 for omega = 4, 8, and 12. The result is a graded rotation-associated longevity hierarchy: weak rotation gives little practical rescue, intermediate rotation substantially extends localization, and the strongest tested branch remains transient-localized through t = 100. Matched-energy near-zero-J_z controls provide a separate causality check and show that net canonical angular momentum alone is not a monotonic explanation of every late-time difference. Stage B2 separately tests spontaneous self-spin from exactly zero initial total angular momentum and finds no validated convergent counter-rotating branch in the tested scalar-only initial-data families. The ordered scan supports a physical formation picture in which a localized grain can move from weak rotational asymmetry through progressive spin-up into a strong-rotation long-lived branch. Time, space, and omega are dimensionless reduced-branch quantities; t = 100 is not assigned an SI duration in this work. The deposit contains the Version 1.0 manuscript PDF, a reproducibility ZIP with the publication source, code, selected archived numerical outputs, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity manifest. The final main.pdf is the default preview. License: Enchan Research & Verification License v1.0. Copyright (c) 2026 Mitsuhiro Kobayashi.

summary: This work studies whether internal rotation changes the longevity of source-free localized excitations in the reduced Enchan local time-rate field. The frozen scalar dynamics are S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with D = |grad S| and mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)); no continuing external torque, centrifugal force, primitive matter source, or added rotational potential is used during the reported evolutions. Stage A supplies the non-rotating source-free baseline. Stage B1 initializes rotating phase-space states at omega = 4, 8, and 12 and evolves the extended runs to dimensionless time t = 100. Over 80 <= t <= 100, the mean localized-energy fractions are approximately 0.002207 for the non-rotating baseline and 0.006006, 0.149470, and 0.368846 for omega = 4, 8, and 12. The result is a graded rotation-associated longevity hierarchy: weak rotation gives little practical rescue, intermediate rotation substantially extends localization, and the strongest tested branch remains transient-localized through t = 100. Matched-energy near-zero-J_z controls provide a separate causality check and show that net canonical angular momentum alone is not a monotonic explanation of every late-time difference. Stage B2 separately tests spontaneous self-spin from exactly zero initial total angular momentum and finds no validated convergent counter-rotating branch in the tested scalar-only initial-data families. The ordered scan supports a physical formation picture in which a localized grain can move from weak rotational asymmetry through progressive spin-up into a strong-rotation long-lived branch. Time, space, and omega are dimensionless reduced-branch quantities; t = 100 is not assigned an SI duration in this work. summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. PIEZO1 PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.edr TRPM4 TRPM4_Stretch_R1.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R1.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R1.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R2.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R2.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R2.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R3.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R3.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R3.edr Data Usage The trajectory (.xtc) and coordinate (.pdb) files can be analysed using standard molecular dynamics software, including GROMACS, VMD, and PyMOL. The (.edr) files are also provided for energy calculations and to be utilized -b 0 -e 50000 (time 0 - 50 ns) These simulations support quantitative analyses described in the associated publication. PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress via permeation-independent structural adaptation and calcium-dependent cytoskeletal reinforcement. Cell Press Blue. (2026). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpblue.2026.100128

summary: Industry 4.0 transforms manufacturing through cyber-physical systems, the Industrial Internet of Things, digital twins, and data-driven intelligence, yet the volume of latency-sensitive data these technologies generate strains conventional cloud-only computing. Edge and fog computing have emerged as the central enabling paradigm, distributing computation across a device–fog–cloud continuum. This paper surveys the enabling technologies of Industry 4.0 with an emphasis on edge–cloud computing and formulates the resulting computation-offloading problem as a constrained, load-dependent optimization model that jointly minimizes task latency and device energy under deadline and capacity constraints. A genetic algorithm and a particle swarm optimizer are developed and benchmarked against five baseline strategies on synthetic industrial workloads. Across one hundred tasks averaged over ten instances, the genetic algorithm reduced the weighted objective by 34.1 percent relative to a greedy heuristic and by 82.6 percent relative to cloud-only execution, while lowering deadline violations to 1.6 percent. The latency–energy trade-off, convergence, and scalability are analyzed, and managerial implications for industrial deployment are discussed.
title: Energy- and Latency-Aware Computation Offloading in Edge–Fog–Cloud Architectures for Industry 4.0

summary: Supplementary material for the manuscript Li Bai Says Xiangsi and Du Fu Does Not: Idioms of Longing in Tang Poetry and the Lexical Basis of an Emotion Label by Zizheng Lv (Honours Program, Department of Asian Studies, University of British Columbia). The study asks what the yearning label of the Chinese Classical Poetry Dataset (CCPD) measures when a classifier trained on it rates Li Bai far above Du Fu. On held-out benchmark poems the label is recoverable from the words xiangsi (相思) and xiangyi (相忆); in a source-audited corpus of 52,253 Tang poems, xiangsi is followed as a formula with a history, from pre-Tang song to Tang poems of farewell and exchange, across 116 poets, and into fifteen close readings. Contents of Supplementary_Material.zip data/poems_table.parquet : the 52,253 author-eligible, CCPD-training-disjoint Tang poems (chinese-poetry, MIT) with source pointers, normalized and original bodies, poem families, surface forms, the frozen classifier's yearning probability and decision, per-poem counts of the words in the lexicon of longing, and title flags. data/author_dates.csv , data/author_dates_by_poem.csv , data/author_date_supplement.json : author dating for the Tang diachrony (Chinese Text Project Data Wiki plus listed corrections). data/xiangsi_poems_by_title_type.csv , data/dufu_yi_news_poems_by_title_type.csv : every title behind the title-type analyses with its rule-based type. data/literary_case_register.json : source-linked records for the fifteen readings. evidence/ : the numbers behind every figure and statement (benchmark counts and coefficients, corpus rates, lexicon rates with family-bootstrap intervals, diachrony, position, addressee, per-character logit attributions, form standardization, per-author tables for 116 poets, song-title rates). contextual_comparison/ : protocol and results of the three GuwenBERT fine-tuning runs. provenance/ : source versions, permissions, licenses, historical sources, and SHA-256 hashes of the archive inputs. scripts/ , figure_source/ : analysis and rendering code; requirements.txt lists the versions used. file_manifest.json and verify_results.py : SHA-256 integrity check for every distributed file (run python verify_results.py ). What runs from this package. scripts/b_e1_lexicon.py , scripts/d_e3_e4_e6.py and scripts/g_e7_all_poets.py recompute their evidence files from the distributed poem table, and figure_source/render_figures.py renders Figures 1 to 6 from the evidence files. scripts/c_e2_diachrony.py and scripts/h_e8_southern_song.py additionally require the Daizhige transcription of Lu Qinli's pre-Tang anthology and the CText Data Wiki RDF release; scripts/e_e5_attribution.py requires the fitted CCPD pipeline; scripts/a_build_table.py documents how the poem table was derived from the archive. These inputs are third-party or too large to redistribute; the README section External inputs gives their expected locations, and each script stops with a message naming any missing input. Licensing. The author's own contributions in this package (code, evidence files, the poem table's derived columns, the case register, and documentation) are released under CC BY 4.0. Retained third-party notices continue to apply to the respective upstream materials: the poem texts derive from the MIT-licensed chinese-poetry repository, whose notice is included; the birth and death years in data/author_dates.csv and data/author_dates_by_poem.csv derive from the Chinese Text Project Data Wiki and remain under its CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 license, with the author's corrections listed separately in data/author_date_supplement.json . CCPD annotations, fitted model weights, and GuwenBERT checkpoints are not redistributed.

summary: Code, retained reference inputs and derived data for a computational feasibility study of HGD editing in alkaptonuria. The shared-screen comparison retains 70 fixed canonical prime configurations and adds 79 PE3 configurations; with the constant base arm, representation is 110 versus 188 variants. The 93 already-canonical pairs are preserved, so no-loss is structural under common screens. Includes sequence reconstruction, sensitivity analyses and separately recorded panel follow-up computations. No biological experiments or educational-outcome measurements have been performed. Core reproduction and optional dependency scope are documented in verification records. summary: State observation over the Hamilton division algebra is formulated as a structured realization problem for quaternionic multi-input multi-output systems. A left-intertwiner equation unifies companion assignment, row-oriented robust pole assignment, and coupled target realization with explicit noncommutative product order. A unitary measured-subspace decomposition yields a derivative-free observer with n-r dynamic quaternion states, where r = rank C, and reduces observability and detectability to a smaller pair. This order is minimal within the stated quaternion-linear full-state observer class. For full-order observers, structured H2 Lyapunov equations and an exact fixed-target gradient allow noise attenuation without moving the spectrum. For minimum-order observers, the reconstruction exposes the direct noise term and its interaction with pole-invariant injection freedom. Discrete-time formulas include the finite contribution of direct feedthrough, and correlated redundant outputs are characterized as noise references. Reproducible studies verify the gradients, compare quaternion, structured-complex, and real representations, expose the noise-cost nonuniqueness of maximum-volume designs, and test coupled repeated-class targets and a multi-output minimum-order observer.
title: Full- and Minimum-Order Quaternionic MIMO Observers: Spectral Assignment and Noise Geometry

summary: This repository contains the data, documentation, and replication materials associated with the data paper on the  Cartulario de Santo Toribio de Liébana . The dataset provides a structured reconstruction of the documentary collection edited by Luis Sánchez Belda and converts the information contained in the cartulary into machine-readable research data. It covers 566 documentary acts and includes linked information on 576 payment or counter-performance elements, 603 place names, and 1,348 identified persons , together with a concordance between documentary numbering systems. The package preserves the documentary structure of the source while providing standardized variables suitable for quantitative and computational historical research. Particular attention is given to economic transactions. Payments and other forms of material counter-performance are recorded at the individual-component level rather than collapsed into a single transaction value. The data also distinguish operative contractual provisions from penalty clauses and other formulaic diplomatic material. Contains the materials required to reproduce and audit the construction of the dataset, including the structured datasets, extraction and coding documentation, variable definitions, provenance information, validation materials, and the code used for data processing and quality-control procedures. The replication workflow documents the transformation from the published documentary source to the final structured tables. It records corrections and normalization decisions while maintaining traceability to the underlying documentary act. The package is therefore intended not only to reproduce the published dataset but also to make individual coding decisions auditable. The dataset is designed for reuse in research on medieval economic history, property transactions, monastic institutions, historical geography, social networks, and computational approaches to diplomatic sources.
title: Replication package for the Santo Toribio de Liébana medieval cartulary dataset

summary: Background: Dried Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula Retz.) fruit, Dried Amalaki ( Phyllanthus emblica L.) fruit, Dried Vidanga ( Embelia ribes Burm.f.) fruit, Dried Trivruta ( Operculina turpethum (L.) Silva Manso) root and Dried Haridra ( Curcuma longa L.) rhizome; These drugs require reliable diagnostic characteristics for authentication and quality control for use in treatment of Dadru (dermatophytosis) . This study comparatively evaluated their organoleptic, macroscopic, and powder-microscopic characteristics to identify key diagnostic features. Materials and Methods: Authenticated samples of Haritaki, Amalaki, Vidanga, Trivruta and Haridra were evaluated for their organoleptic, macroscopic and powder microscopic characteristics using standard pharmacognostical methods. Diagnostic features were documented by light microscopy and compared with pharmacopoeial references . Results: Pharmacognostical evaluation of Haritaki , Amalaki , Vidanga , Trivruta and Haridra confirmed their authenticity through organoleptic, macroscopic and powder microscopic examinations. Each drug exhibited distinct diagnostic features such as characteristic taste, odour, fracture, and microscopic markers including fibres, stone cells, starch grains, sclereids, vessels and oleoresin cells, consistent with pharmacopeial standards. Conclusion: The study established reproducible diagnostic parameters for the selected drugs, ensuring accurate identification and quality control. These findings provide baseline pharmacognostical data for quality assessment of the selected drugs intended for formulations used in Dadru (dermatophytosis).
tags: Authentication, Microscopy, Pharmacognosy, Powder, Quality control.
title: PHARMACOGNOSTIC CHARACTERIZATION OF HARITAKI, AMALAKI, VIDANGA, TRIVRUTA AND HARIDRA BY ORGANOLEPTIC, MACROSCOPIC AND POWDER MICROSCOPIC STUDIES
Replication package for the article "Market Reactions to European Commission Policy Announcements: A Model Intervention Analysis"

summary: R code, input parameters and generated outputs reproducing every result of the accompanying article. The analysis is a decision-analytic state-transition (Markov) model comparing four strategies for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, aficamten, mavacamten, alcohol septal ablation and septal myectomy, in Germany and the United States, with standard medical therapy as a secondary reference arm. It covers the four-strategy efficiency frontier, four separately defined annual acquisition-price thresholds, probabilistic sensitivity analysis over 10 000 draws with common random numbers, and an age-specific specification for starting ages 40 to 85 years using national life tables and published age-stratified procedural risks. Contents: 16 R scripts, two life-table input files, and 70 generated outputs (tables, figures and logs). Running "Rscript run_all.R" from a clean directory regenerates all of them. The run begins with an audit gate of 252 automated checks covering arithmetic identities, the provenance of every price, the separation of the four price concepts, the wording of categorical results, and the internal consistency of the cross-trial declaration. No output is written unless every check passes. No individual patient data are included or required. All inputs are published trial results, national tariff catalogues, national life tables and explicitly declared assumptions; each is listed with its source, or with the explicit absence of one, in the provenance register. Requires R 4.6.0 or later with ggplot2, dplyr, scales, patchwork, ggrepel and jsonlite.
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Myosin Inhibitors and Septal Reduction Therapies for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

summary: Unofficial Gujarati (gu-Gujr-IN) machine-assisted translation of the Open Logic Project, frozen at revision 9620cc73f9c8e0ad003c514a5d3748f29611c4c0. This cumulative release covers 163 of the 722 tracked content units, OLP-0004–OLP-0166. It contains complete Sets, Relations, Functions, Size of Sets, Arithmetization, Infinite Sets, Propositional Logic syntax and semantics, the first-order proof-systems overview, Sequent Calculus, Natural Deduction, signed analytic Tableaux, Axiomatic Deduction, First-Order Completeness, the First-Order Logic introduction, Syntax, and Semantics. The new semantics chapter develops structures and universes, term values, covered structures, variable assignments, recursive satisfaction, assignment independence, extensionality, validity, consequence, satisfiability, models, and theories. The full Gujarati edition remains in progress. The deposit preserves the exact anonymously verified GitHub release first-order-semantics-v0.10.0 at commit 8e05f9182abbda985f31222a7e2e00a08fec25b9: a 211-page A4 PDF, the cumulative TeX driver, a complete editable source ZIP, a genuine reflowable EPUB 3.3 publication, the offline HTML/MathML reader, SHA-256 checksums, and a machine-readable QA record. The PDF is uploaded first as the human-readable Zenodo preview. The archive contains all 722 pristine English source units as source provenance; only the stated 163 units are translated. Translation and review were performed by a Codex agent. Checks include 1,815 exact aligned linguistic-block reviews, 9,587 source mathematical spans, 829 reverse-paraphrase samples, 117 disclosed frozen-source corrections, three byte-identical PDF passes, visual inspection of all 211 PDF pages, and an offline reader with 9,340 MathML nodes, five truth tables, six line-numbered axiomatic derivation tables, thirteen described diagrams, 208 structural proof representations, 654 unique anchors, and no broken internal links. The EPUB preserves all 9,340 native MathML expressions, 171 navigation links, Gujarati metadata and fonts, described diagrams, and correction disclosures; a byte-identical cold replay, EPUBCheck 5.3.0 with zero messages, and silent Chromium inspection passed. These are same-agent checks, not independent native-speaker or human certification. Some specialized Gujarati terms remain provisional. Eighteen Gujarati scholarly and educational sources and seventy-seven exact passages were directly inspected, with terminology, hash and segment-use indexes included. Copyrighted canon originals and full extracts are excluded. The inherited Open Logic Project attribution and CC BY 4.0 license are preserved; bundled Noto Sans Gujarati font files retain their SIL Open Font License. This translation does not imply endorsement by the source authors or canon publishers.

summary: Derived tables and provenance registries supporting source-resolved mass absorption efficiency (MAE) estimates for wintertime brown carbon from residential solid-fuel and fossil-fuel combustion across European and Chinese sites. Contents: (i) source-resolved MAE estimates for the European station pairs and six Chinese cities with block-bootstrap percentile intervals and trustworthiness grading; (ii) station metadata and the field-level verification status of the Chinese records; (iii) per-dataset variable-group coverage tables and sensitivity analyses; (iv) the 84-field variable dictionary of the harmonized master table; (v) per-dataset provenance registries recording authoritative archives, citations and access routes, including a per-file DOI registry for the EBAS absorption compilation; (vi) the evidence tables underlying the Supporting Information (spectral benchmarks, coverage analyses, validation tables, perturbation domains, and the literature-coordinate conversion audit); (vii) an integrity baseline of file checksums for independent verification. Primary hourly records are not redistributed and are available from the original archives identified in the provenance registry or from the authors on request. The harmonized master table itself is not included. Earlier versions and superseded analyses are documented in the version history; the current release is the curated final set. v1.7.0 (2026-09-20) : third-round revision-companion update. Adds the pricing estimand registry (coal: Kraków 2018/19 pure-CCOA median 4.61 m² g⁻¹; biofuel: five-station winter-matched effective 3.84 m² g⁻¹), the source-omission benchmark with locked-λ bootstrap loss distributions, placebo arms and model-available bulk predictors, the unified canonical interval products and block-length sensitivities, the canonical-construction coverage harness, the conditional-ratio bootstrap draws, the locked SI table mirrors (SI_Table_S26–S31.csv), and the figure-generation and 370 nm conversion scripts. See README_v1.7.0_addendum.md inside the archive for the file-level inventory.

Elle comprend 45 sections, 73 exercices et 51 des 722 unités prévues pour l'édition intégrale. Traduction et révision éditoriale assistées par IA, avec références françaises et décisions documentées. Aucune validation humaine indépendante n'est revendiquée. L'édition intégrale reste en cours. summary: This manuscript identifies six substrates — individual memory, species lineages, externalised records, immune memory, the first generation of stars, and prion populations — which share a four-part mechanical structure, and among which no pair, to our knowledge, cites another. We specify the four mechanisms as an explicit screen, and validate it by applying it to cases that should fail: thermal equilibrium scores zero of four, sheared amorphous matter scores an intermediate two and a half, and stem cells score three of four in a manner that identifies precisely which mechanism is missing. We then derive, from this framework’s own commitment that any render of a record is necessarily partial, a scaling law governing all six: the more degraded the record, the more the reconstruction is determined by the template rather than by the record. We show this law is independently confirmed in four of the six fields, under four different names, by researchers not addressing one another. We supply a birth term that a companion manuscript’s earlier treatment lacked, deriving it from Bennett’s history-tape result rather than from biology, and show that a standard macroevolutionary survivorship formula then applies to memory unchanged. Three results that did not hold are recorded in full, including one prediction that failed outright on simulation and one correspondence that was stated backwards relative to the data. The foundational architecture, geometric intuitions, and motivating philosophy of this framework originated independently with the author prior to and separate from any AI involvement. Subsequent mathematical derivation, connection to established physics literature, computational verification, and error-checking were conducted through extended technical work with AI systems (Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini). The author directed this process, evaluated and selected among proposed derivations, and takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the final work.
title: Reconstruction from a Degraded Record: Six Substrates, One Scaling Law, and a Dispute Six Fields Have Independently

summary: Metrics Added MixtureMetric and MixtureComponent , which express a weighted linear combination of BaseMetric instances. This is exact, by linearity of expectation, and is how empcs_score now expresses a distribution that mixes a point mass with a continuous piece — something a single Metric cannot express, since SymPy cannot symbolically integrate over such a distribution. Added BaseMetric , the abstraction every loss parameter throughout the package now accepts. Metric and MixtureMetric both implement it, so either can be passed interchangeably as a model's training objective. Added the LogCost strategy for building custom expected log cost (weighted cross-entropy) metrics. expected_log_cost_loss is now built from it. Metrics built with the Cost and Savings strategies now accept stochastic ( sympy.stats ) cost parameters, reducing them to their mean. Previously this raised NotImplementedError: Random variables are not supported for the savings metric. at Metric construction time. Added constrain and constrain , which declare the values a cost-matrix parameter is allowed to take. A parameter can be given inclusive lower / upper bounds, or a callable can express a condition spanning several parameters at once ( constrain(lambda p: p['clv'] > p['incentive_cost'], message=...) ). Added Profit , MinCost and EmpiricalMinCost , the sign-flipped siblings of Cost , MaxProfit and EmpiricalMaxProfit . Each computes the same quantity as its partner and reports it with the opposite sign, so a cost matrix can be read as costs to minimize or as profits to maximize. The choice is presentational: the optimal threshold and rate are unchanged, and models fit identically on either member of a pair. Added EmpiricalMaxProfit and AUEPC strategies for building custom metrics that compute the empirical (convex-hull-based) maximum profit and the area under the empirical profit curve, respectively. Metric now warns ( UserWarning ) at construction when the cost matrix has no terms, or its terms cancel to exactly zero — such a metric always evaluates to 0.0 regardless of its parameters. Metric now warns when called with a parameter its cost matrix does not use, instead of silently ignoring it — catching a typo'd keyword argument. sample_weight and strategy-specific extras (e.g. Savings ' baseline ) are exempt. Multi-letter symbols now render upright in the LaTeX representations of CostMatrix and Metric , so a product such as clv * r reads as two variables rather than as one named clvr . Greek names such as gamma are unaffected. MaxProfit with integration_method='auto' now uses quasi-Monte Carlo for any number of stochastic variables whose distributions can be sampled, rather than only above two. Two stochastic variables used to go to nested quadrature. Pass random_state for a result reproducible across Metric instances; repeated calls on one instance were already identical. Deterministic MaxProfit metrics (a profit function polynomial in the stochastic variable) no longer compute the ROC convex hull, and evaluate the profit function vectorized over all operating points instead of in a Python loop. Quasi-Monte Carlo integration now covers eleven more distributions: BoundedPareto , Dagum , ExponentialPower (not published in SymPy's own documentation, so no link is possible), Frechet , Gompertz , LogLogistic , RaisedCosine , Rayleigh , Reciprocal , Weibull and WignerSemicircle . These previously fell through to plain Monte Carlo, which is around a thousand times less accurate for the same sampling budget. optimal_rate and optimal_threshold now always compute the exact EMP when one stochastic variable is present. MaxProfit accepts profit functions of any shape in the stochastic variable. Previously a cost matrix using exp , log or a square root raised PolynomialError from inside SymPy when the Metric was constructed. check_input has been removed from every prebuilt metric that is now a Metric / MixtureMetric instance ( empc_score , mpc_score , empb_score

summary: Invasive plant species pose a significant threat to global biodiversity, particularly within protected areas. This study investigated the diversity, community structure and distribution of invasive plants in Margalla Hills National Park (MHNP), Pakistan, combining a systematic quadrat-based field survey with soil physicochemical analysis and a GIS/remote-sensing framework. Surveys were conducted along 300 m transects, with separate quadrats for trees (10 × 10 m), shrubs (5 × 5 m) and herbs (1 × 1 m). The survey yielded 26 growth-form records representing 24 taxonomically distinct invasive species. Ricinus communis and Annona squamosa were each recorded as both a tree and a shrub. Overall records comprised 12 tree, 8 shrub and 6 herb growth forms. Because quadrat areas differed among growth forms, density was standardized to individuals m⁻² for cross-form comparison, on which basis herbs were by far the densest (5.19 m⁻²), followed by shrubs (0.77 m⁻²) and trees (0.14 m⁻²). Within growth forms, Sophora japonica led the trees (26.54 individuals quadrat⁻¹), Tecoma stans the shrubs (20.90) and Silybum marianum the herbs (5.58). Herbs also recorded the highest mean cover (24.99 ± 6.61%). Across the park, Broussonetia papyrifera, Parthenium hysterophorus and Lantana camara were the most frequently recorded dominants. The invasive assemblage was most species-rich and diverse in the tree layer (Shannon–Wiener H ≈ 2.52) and least diverse in the herb layer (≈ 1.98), reflecting the broad suite of woody invaders established in the park and the sustained pressure this places on native woody communities. Soils were neutral to slightly acidic (pH 6.63–7.22) with low electrical conductivity (0.81 dS m⁻¹) and very low organic matter (0.13 ± 0.01%), conditions associated with hardy, disturbance-adapted invaders. These findings confirm active invasion across all growth forms and provide a spatially explicit baseline for targeted management and long-term monitoring of this protected Himalayan ecosystem.
title: Community structure, edaphic drivers and ecological impacts of invasive plant species in Margalla Hills National Park, Pakistan

summary: Hashing Is Not Retrieval is a prospectively frozen three-arm evaluation of context accumulation in small-model multi-agent code cartography. It compares three ways for an orchestrator to hand work to a worker: 1. FULL HISTORY — retransmit prior worker outputs. 2. OPAQUE REF — replace the previous output with an unretrievable SHA-256 digest. 3. RETRIEVED — resolve the digest through a tenant-scoped content-addressed store and inject the recovered bytes. All arms receive identical source-derived evidence. The apparatus measures the exact message content sent to workers and records token counts, model and provider identifiers, generation IDs, usage, cost, retries, and retrieval proofs. A five-task gate preceded a fixed 50-task controlled benchmark, followed by a separate state-required evaluation across 24 deterministic fixtures and a five-scale Medusa case study. Key result: in the controlled benchmark, RETRIEVED reduced paired peak context by 38.3% relative to FULL HISTORY. The state-required follow-up shows that opaque references fail when state must be recovered, while verified retrieval preserves substantially more structural information. This is bounded-context evidence for automatic orchestrator-resolved state passing inside a specific two-worker code-cartography harness — not a universal claim about autonomous memory, long-context capability, or reasoning quality. The release includes the corrected author-identified preprint, executable apparatus, frozen results, task fixtures, telemetry, and verification instructions. Version 1.0.2 supplies the curated, verifier-passing reproducibility archive. It supersedes the uncurated archive from version 1.0.1 and includes the exact pinned apparatus, state-required fixtures, frozen results, and archive verifier. Submission status: This preprint was submitted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Long Context Foundation Models (LCFM). LCFM is a non-archival workshop; this Zenodo record is a public preprint and does not indicate acceptance or publication. Workshop information: https://longcontextfm.github.io/ Research website: https://abdulmoizahmed.com/research Concept DOI (all versions): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22844754 License: CC BY 4.0.
